scenario: Deuce court, 40-30. You've won three straight points serving wide, but on that last one the returner started a metre wider and took it early crosscourt. Where do you serve now?
options: Serve T into the space they left
Serve wide again, harder this time
Serve at their body to jam them
explanation: They have shown the adjustment — a metre wider and stepping in — so the T they abandoned is now free space. Serving wide again with more pace fires straight into the ball they just repositioned to hit.
takeaway: Repeat a winning serve until they move, then serve where they moved from.

scenario: Ad court, 30-30. Your wide serve is blocked back deep and heavy into your backhand corner, and you're a metre behind the baseline still recovering. What's the +1?
options: Heavy backhand crosscourt and reset
Run around it for an inside-out forehand
Backhand down the line into the open court
explanation: A deep return kills the +1, so height and depth crosscourt buy back the recovery step you owe. Running around for the inside-out forehand is the trap: it opens the whole ad side while you are still moving backwards.
takeaway: Deep return, no +1 — reset crosscourt and earn the next ball.

scenario: Third set at 4-4. Your first-serve percentage has fallen from 60% to 35% since the second-set tiebreak, and your legs are gone even though the arm feels fine. First fix?
options: Take 10% off the pace and add spin
Keep the pace but aim well inside the lines
Keep the pace and go bigger to end points
explanation: Tired legs shorten the kinetic chain, so full pace flattens the trajectory and the ball clips the tape; less pace with spin restores the arc. Keeping the pace and aiming safer fails because your aim was never the problem.
takeaway: When the legs go, trade pace for arc.

scenario: Your opponent stands far back to return second serves. What's the best second serve choice?
options: A kick serve that jumps above shoulder height
A slow slice wide
A flat T serve
explanation: A deep returner is vulnerable to high-bouncing balls that force upward contact from shoulder height or above.
takeaway: When they stand deep, bounce the ball up — don't dink it in.
scenarioTr: Rakip ikinci servisleri çok geriden karşılıyor. En iyi ikinci servis seçimi nedir?
optionsTr: Omuz hizasının üstüne sıçrayan kick servis
explanationTr: Geride duran rakip, omuz hizasından yukarı vurmak zorunda kaldığı yüksek sıçrayan toplara karşı zayıftır.
takeawayTr: Geride duruyorlarsa topu sıçrat — ortaya atmadan.
scenarioFr: Ton adversaire se place très loin derrière pour retourner les deuxièmes balles. Quel est le meilleur choix ?
optionsFr: Un service kické qui rebondit au-dessus de l'épaule
Un slice lent à l'extérieur
Un service à plat au T
explanationFr: Un relanceur très reculé est vulnérable aux balles à rebond haut qui l'obligent à frapper au-dessus de l'épaule.
takeawayFr: Quand il recule, fais rebondir haut — ne pousse pas la balle.

scenario: 30-40, the first break point you've faced this set. Your opponent has stepped inside the baseline on five of your last six second serves and won three of those points.
options: First serve at 80%, spin, at the body
First serve flat down the T for the ace
First serve wide and follow it to the net
explanation: With the returner camped inside the baseline, the ball to avoid is a second serve, so an 80% spin first serve that jams the body is worth more than pace. Going flat for the T ace fails here — the miss hands them exactly what they want.
takeaway: On break point, make the first serve — the miss is the real risk.
mistakeType: going for too much on break point

scenario: A right-handed opponent stands slightly closer to the alley in the ad court. What serve exploits this?
options: T serve into their backhand
Wide slice to their forehand
Body serve at their feet
explanation: Shifting toward the alley opens the T completely, forcing a jammed backhand return.
takeaway: Read returner positioning before every serve — adjust to their stance, not yours.
scenarioTr: Ad tarafta sağlak rakip korte biraz daha yakın duruyor. Hangi servis bunu cezalandırır?
explanationTr: Kort kenarına kayması T'yi tam olarak açar ve sıkışmış bir backhand dönüşü zorlar.
takeawayTr: Her servis öncesi karşıladığı pozisyonu oku — kendine göre değil ona göre servis at.
scenarioFr: Un adversaire droitier se place un peu plus près du couloir côté avantage. Quel service exploite ça ?
optionsFr: Service au T dans son revers
Slice extérieur sur son coup droit
Service sur le corps, dans les pieds
explanationFr: En se décalant vers le couloir, il ouvre complètement le T et se retrouve coincé sur un retour de revers.
takeawayFr: Lis le placement du relanceur avant chaque service — adapte-toi à sa position, pas à la tienne.

scenario: 5-3, serving for the set at 30-15. You've held every service game this set with the same wide-then-T pattern in the deuce court, and the returner still hasn't covered it.
options: Keep running the wide-then-T pattern
Switch to serves you haven't shown them yet
Serve everything at the body to stay safe
explanation: The pattern has held every game because the returner has not solved it, and the last game of a set is no time to test unproven targets. Switching to serves you haven't shown is tempting variety with no evidence behind it.
takeaway: Close the set with the pattern that built it.

scenario: You're playing a tall opponent with long arms who returns both wide serves comfortably. What's the pattern adjustment?
options: Serve into the body to jam the swing
Serve even wider to stretch them
Serve shorter for lower bounce
explanation: Tall players with reach cover wide serves well. A body serve removes their reach advantage and forces a cramped swing.
takeaway: Against long-armed players, crowd them — don't stretch them.
scenarioTr: Uzun kollu ve her iki açık servisi rahat karşılayan uzun bir rakiple oynuyorsun. Desen ayarı ne olmalı?
optionsTr: Vurmayı sıkıştırmak için vücuda servis at
Daha da geniş at, onları gerebilmek için
Düşük sıçrama için daha kısa at
explanationTr: Uzun kollu oyuncular açık servisleri iyi kapsar. Vücut servisi uzunluk avantajını ortadan kaldırır.
takeawayTr: Uzun kollulara karşı gerdirme — sıkıştır.
scenarioFr: Tu joues contre un adversaire grand, aux bras longs, qui retourne facilement les services extérieurs. Quel ajustement ?
optionsFr: Servir sur le corps pour bloquer son geste
Servir encore plus extérieur pour l'étirer
Servir plus court pour un rebond bas
explanationFr: Les grands joueurs couvrent bien l'extérieur grâce à leur allonge. Un service sur le corps annule cet avantage et coince leur geste.
takeawayFr: Contre des bras longs, colle-le — ne l'étire pas.

scenario: 30-30 in the deuce court, one point after a double fault. Your first serve has landed 65% all match; the fault came on a second serve you decelerated into.
options: Your normal first serve, full swing
Roll a 70% first serve in to be sure
Flatten it out and go for the ace
explanation: The evidence says your first serve is healthy and the fault came from deceleration, so a full normal swing is the lowest-risk ball available. Rolling in a 70% first serve is the tempting fix, but decelerating is what just failed you.
takeaway: After a double, swing fully at your normal first serve.

scenario: Second set, serving into a steady headwind on this end. Your kick second serves have been landing short and sitting up mid-box, and the returner has started stepping in on them.
options: Toss lower and in front, hit deeper
Add more spin and keep the same target
Toss higher and swing softer for control
explanation: A headwind brakes the ball and steals length, so a lower toss in front and a deeper, flatter target puts the serve back on the line. Adding more spin is the instinct that fails: it drops the serve even shorter into their strike zone.
takeaway: Into the wind: lower toss, deeper target.

scenario: 0-30 up on their serve, but they've just hit two 190 km/h first serves at your backhand and you're blocking from a metre behind the baseline. Where does this block go?
options: Deep down the middle, high over the net
Deep crosscourt, away from their forehand
Low and short to drag them forward
explanation: Blocking from behind the baseline you can't control a sideline, and a deep middle ball takes away the server's angle while you recover. Deep crosscourt looks just as safe but leaks wide off a stretched block and opens the court.
takeaway: Stretched block: high, deep, down the middle.

scenario: Your opponent's first serve averages below 160 km/h. Where should you stand to return?
options: Inside the baseline to take time away
Two steps behind the baseline to give yourself time
Same spot as for a big server
explanation: Against slower serves, stepping inside the baseline takes time away from the server's next shot and pressures them immediately.
takeaway: Return position is a weapon — match it to the server's pace.
scenarioTr: Rakibin ilk servis ortalaması 160 km/h'nin altında. Karşılamak için nerede durmalısın?
optionsTr: Kaleden iki adım geride — zaman kazan
Büyük servisçiye karşı olduğu gibi aynı yer
explanationTr: Yavaş servislere karşı kaleden öne adım atmak rakibin sonraki vuruşundan zaman çalar.
takeawayTr: Karşılama pozisyonu silahtır — servisçinin hızına göre ayarla.
scenarioFr: La première balle de ton adversaire tourne sous les 160 km/h. Où te places-tu pour retourner ?
optionsFr: À l'intérieur de la ligne de fond pour lui voler du temps
Deux pas derrière la ligne pour te donner du temps
Au même endroit que face à un gros serveur
explanationFr: Face à un service plus lent, avancer dans le court enlève du temps au serveur pour son coup suivant et le met immédiatement sous pression.
takeawayFr: La position de retour est une arme — règle-la sur la vitesse du serveur.

scenario: Before the serve, what should you be mentally committed to?
options: A specific target zone for the return
Whatever shot feels right at contact
Just getting it back in play
explanation: Decisions made before contact are calmer and cleaner. Reactive decisions at contact lead to tentative swings.
takeaway: Decide the return direction before the ball leaves the server's hand.
scenarioTr: Servis atılmadan önce zihinsel olarak neye söz vermiş olmalısın?
optionsTr: Dönüş için belirli bir hedef bölgesi
explanationTr: Temas öncesi verilen kararlar daha sakin ve temizdir. Temas anında verilen tepkisel kararlar tereddütlü vuruşlara yol açar.
takeawayTr: Dönüş yönüne servis atılmadan önce karar ver.
scenarioFr: Avant le service, sur quoi dois-tu être mentalement engagé ?
optionsFr: Une zone cible précise pour ton retour
Le coup qui te semblera juste à l'impact
Juste remettre la balle en jeu
explanationFr: Une décision prise avant l'impact est plus calme et plus nette. Décider au moment de la frappe mène à des gestes hésitants.
takeawayFr: Choisis la direction du retour avant que la balle quitte la main du serveur.

scenario: On ad court, the server hits a wide kick serve jumping to your backhand. Best target?
options: A high block return crosscourt and deep
A down-the-line attempted winner
A drop shot
explanation: A high-bouncing wide kick serve is a poor ball to attack. Neutralising crosscourt gives you time to recover the middle.
takeaway: Against kick serves pulling you off court, reset — don't counterpunch.
scenarioTr: Ad tarafta servisçi backhand'e yükselen açık kick servis attı. En iyi hedef?
explanationTr: Yüksek sıçrayan açık kick servis saldırılacak bir top değildir. Çaprazlama nötürlemek toparlanma zamanı verir.
takeawayTr: Seni korttan çıkaran kick servislere karşı sıfırla — karşı atak yapma.
scenarioFr: Côté avantage, le serveur sort un service kické extérieur qui saute sur ton revers. Meilleure cible ?
optionsFr: Un retour bloqué haut, croisé et profond
Un long de ligne tenté en gagnant
Une amortie
explanationFr: Un kické extérieur à rebond haut est une mauvaise balle à attaquer. Neutraliser en croisé te laisse le temps de revenir au centre.
takeawayFr: Sur un kické qui te sort du court, remets-toi en jeu — ne contre pas.

scenario: When should your split step land as the server makes contact?
options: Just before the server hits the ball
Exactly as the serve is hit
After you see the ball direction
explanation: Landing just before contact means your feet are about to touch the ground as the serve is struck — giving you an explosive push toward the ball.
takeaway: Land into the split just before the hit — not after.
scenarioTr: Split step ne zaman yere inmeli?
explanationTr: Servis vuruşundan hemen önce inmek, ayakların yere değmek üzereyken servisin atılmasıyla patlamalı itme sağlar.
takeawayTr: Split'e servis vuruşundan hemen önce in — sonra değil.
scenarioFr: Quand ton split-step doit-il retomber par rapport à l'impact du serveur ?
optionsFr: Juste avant que le serveur frappe la balle
Exactement au moment de la frappe
Après avoir vu la direction de la balle
explanationFr: Retomber juste avant l'impact met tes pieds au contact du sol au moment où le service part — et te donne une poussée explosive vers la balle.
takeawayFr: Retombe du split juste avant la frappe — pas après.

scenario: Opponent's second serve averages 140 km/h with heavy kick. What's the best aggressive return pattern?
options: Move up and take it on the rise, crosscourt
Move up but go down the line for a winner
Stand back and block it safely
explanation: Moving up denies the kick its bounce height. Driving it crosscourt is the higher-percentage aggressive return — more court length and a lower net give you margin to set up a +1. Down the line is tempting but lower-percentage off a deep kicking ball.
takeaway: Attack a second serve by moving forward — and go crosscourt for margin.
scenarioTr: Rakibin ikinci servisi 140 km/h ağır kick'le geliyor. En iyi agresif dönüş deseni?
optionsTr: Öne gel ama winner için çizgiye git
explanationTr: Öne gelmek kick'in sıçrama yüksekliğini yok eder. Çapraz sürmek daha yüksek yüzdeli agresif dönüştür — daha uzun saha ve daha alçak file +1 kurmak için sana pay verir. Çizgiye vurmak cazip ama derin kick'li topta daha düşük yüzdeli.
takeawayTr: İkinci servise saldırmak için öne gel — ve pay için çapraz git.
scenarioFr: La deuxième balle adverse tourne à 140 km/h avec beaucoup de kick. Quel est le meilleur schéma de retour agressif ?
optionsFr: Avancer et la prendre à la montée, en croisé
Avancer mais tenter le long de ligne gagnant
Rester derrière et bloquer prudemment
explanationFr: Avancer prive le kick de sa hauteur de rebond. La frapper en croisé est le retour agressif le plus rentable — plus de longueur de court et un filet plus bas te donnent la marge pour enchaîner le +1. Le long de ligne est tentant, mais moins rentable sur une balle kickée profonde.
takeawayFr: Attaque une deuxième balle en avançant — et joue croisé pour la marge.

scenario: You've just hit a deep crosscourt return to a righty's backhand in the deuce court, and they're stretched behind their own baseline. Where do you recover to before their contact?
options: A step to the crosscourt side
Straight back to the exact centre mark
Shade toward the down-the-line side
explanation: A stretched backhand from behind the baseline comes back crosscourt far more often than down the line, so bisecting their real angles means shading that way. Recovering to the exact centre mark is the default that ignores this ball.
takeaway: Recover to their likely reply, not to the centre mark.

scenario: Against a server who is slow at the baseline, when is a chip-and-charge return smart?
options: On a predictable second serve in a 30-0 situation
On every first serve
Only on break points
explanation: Chip-and-charge on a predictable second serve at 30-0 puts the slow-baseline opponent in a passing-shot situation they're uncomfortable in — without risking a critical score.
takeaway: Chip-and-charge works in low-stakes moments against predictable serves.
scenarioTr: Kaleden yavaş olan servisçiye karşı chip-and-charge dönüşü ne zaman akıllıca?
explanationTr: 30-0'da tahmin edilebilir ikinci servise chip-and-charge, kaleden yavaş rakibi zorlayan bir passing-shot durumuna sokar — kritik skor riski almadan.
takeawayTr: Chip-and-charge tahmin edilebilir servislere ve düşük riskli anlara yakışır.
scenarioFr: Face à un serveur lent en fond de court, quand le retour coupé-montée est-il intelligent ?
optionsFr: Sur une deuxième balle prévisible à 30-0
Sur chaque première balle
Uniquement sur les balles de break
explanationFr: Le retour coupé-montée sur une deuxième balle prévisible à 30-0 met un adversaire lent en fond de court dans une situation de passing qu'il n'aime pas — sans risquer un score critique.
takeawayFr: Le coupé-montée marche dans les moments à faible enjeu, contre un service prévisible.

scenario: Returning at 4-5, 30-30, you arrive at the return spot still holding your breath from the last rally. Where in the server's ritual does your exhale belong?
options: As they start bouncing the ball
As their racquet meets the ball
While you walk back to the line
explanation: Breathing out on the ball bounces releases tension while you still have time to load the split step, and it finishes before the toss needs your eyes. Exhaling at their contact is too late — you read and move on a held breath.
takeaway: Breathe out on their bounces, split on their contact.

scenario: 15-40 on their serve, two break points in hand. They've missed the first serve on six of the last eight points and the second sits up at 130 km/h.
options: Attack the first break point hardest
Play the first deep, attack only the second
Play both deep and make them win the points
explanation: The first break point is where the server is most likely to miss the first serve, so spend the aggression there instead of saving it. Playing the first deep and neutral hands back the very ball you earned the chance to attack.
takeaway: Spend the first break point, don't save it.

scenario: You're in a neutral crosscourt rally with even positioning. What's the default plan?
options: Keep hitting crosscourt with depth and wait for a short ball
Change direction to break the pattern
Hit harder to force the error
explanation: Crosscourt is the safest trajectory — lowest net, deepest landing zone. Direction change is a choice for short balls, not neutral exchanges.
takeaway: Crosscourt until the ball says otherwise.
scenarioTr: Pozisyonlar eşit, nötr çapraz rally içindesin. Varsayılan plan ne?
optionsTr: Çapraz derinlik at ve kısa top bekle
Hatayı zorlamak için daha sert vur
explanationTr: Çapraz en güvenli yörüngedir — en düşük file, en derin iniş alanı. Yön değişimi kısa toplar için bir seçimdir, nötrler için değil.
takeawayTr: Top aksini söyleyene kadar çapraz.
scenarioFr: Tu es dans un échange croisé neutre, positions équilibrées. Quel est le plan par défaut ?
optionsFr: Continuer en croisé avec de la profondeur et attendre la balle courte
Changer de direction pour casser le schéma
Frapper plus fort pour provoquer la faute
explanationFr: Le croisé est la trajectoire la plus sûre : filet le plus bas, zone d'atterrissage la plus longue. Le changement de direction se décide sur une balle courte, pas dans un échange neutre.
takeawayFr: Croisé, jusqu'à ce que la balle dise le contraire.

scenario: Your opponent keeps sending high, looping topspin to your backhand. What's the best counter?
options: Move inside the baseline and take it on the rise
Retreat to the fence and loop it back
Slice it low and short
explanation: Moonballs rely on time. Taking it on the rise inside the baseline removes that time and turns their defensive shot into your attacking one.
takeaway: Don't let a moonball push you back — step forward instead.
scenarioTr: Rakip sürekli backhand'ine yüksek topspin topu atıyor. En iyi karşı hamle?
optionsTr: Kalenin içine gel ve yükseliyorken vur
Çite kadar geri çekil ve lupla
explanationTr: Moonball zamanın üzerinde çalışır. Kalenin içinde yükseliyorken vurmak o zamanı elinden alır ve savunma toplarını saldırı toplarına çevirir.
takeawayTr: Moonball seni geriye itmesin — öne adım at.
scenarioFr: Ton adversaire t'envoie sans arrêt des balles hautes et liftées sur le revers. Quelle est la meilleure réponse ?
optionsFr: Avancer dans le court et la prendre à la montée
Reculer jusqu'au grillage et la relober
La slicer bas et court
explanationFr: Les balles hautes fonctionnent grâce au temps qu'elles donnent. La prendre à la montée dans le court supprime ce temps et transforme sa balle défensive en ton attaque.
takeawayFr: Ne laisse pas une balle haute te repousser — avance.

scenario: It's 4–4, deuce, and you've just dragged a heavy crosscourt forehand from well outside the deuce sideline. Your opponent takes it early and loves the down-the-line change. Where do you recover to?
options: A step ad-side of the centre mark
The centre mark, square to the middle
Stay wide and guard the line you left
explanation: Because your contact was outside the sideline, the two replies they can reach bisect on the ad side of centre, so a step past the mark covers both. The centre mark leaves you a stride late on anything into the ad court.
takeaway: Recover to the middle of their angles, not the middle of the court.

scenario: You're more fit than your opponent. What's the smart rally-length strategy?
options: Extend rallies with high margin and safe depth
Shorten rallies with aggressive first-strike tennis
Serve and volley every point
explanation: Fitness advantage compounds over long rallies. Making your opponent play one more ball than they're comfortable with multiplies over a match.
takeaway: Use fitness as a tactic — don't just survive, extend.
scenarioTr: Rakibinden daha iyi kondisyondasın. Akıllı rally uzunluğu stratejisi ne?
optionsTr: Yüksek marjla ve güvenli derinlikle rally'leri uzat
explanationTr: Kondisyon avantajı uzun rally'lerde katlanır. Rakibin rahat olduğundan bir top fazla oynatmak maç boyunca çarpan etkisi yapar.
takeawayTr: Kondisyonu taktik yap — sadece hayatta kalmakla kalma, uzat.
scenarioFr: Tu es plus en forme physiquement que ton adversaire. Quelle stratégie de longueur d'échange ?
optionsFr: Allonger les échanges avec de la marge et de la profondeur
Raccourcir les échanges en attaquant d'entrée
Servir-volée sur chaque point
explanationFr: L'avantage physique se cumule sur les échanges longs. Faire jouer une balle de plus que ce qui est confortable se multiplie sur la durée d'un match.
takeawayFr: Sers-toi de ta condition comme d'une tactique — ne te contente pas de survivre, allonge.

scenario: Third set, 2–3, legs heavy. You're a metre behind the baseline and your last four forehands came off the frame, each one struck as the ball dropped past your hip.
options: Turn earlier, contact out in front
Back up a metre and let it drop
Step in and take it on the rise
explanation: Fatigue slows the feet, not the swing, so turning earlier restores a contact point in front where the frame stops appearing. Backing up feels safer but adds a step of running and drops contact even further behind you.
takeaway: Tired legs: turn earlier, don't reach later.
mistakeType: reaching for the ball when tired

scenario: You hit a strong deep ball and your opponent replies with a short mid-court ball. First decision?
options: Move in, load your shot, and plan the +1
Hit it hard as a winner attempt
Play it safe back to middle
explanation: Short balls aren't winners — they're transition opportunities. Move in, load, and plan the next ball rather than forcing a single-shot winner.
takeaway: Short balls are setups, not winners.
scenarioTr: Derin sert bir top attın ve rakip orta kort kısa bir topla yanıtladı. İlk karar?
optionsTr: Öne gel, vuruşunu yükle ve +1'i planla
explanationTr: Kısa toplar winner değildir — geçiş fırsatlarıdır. İçeri gir, yüklen ve tek atışla winner zorlamak yerine sonraki topu planla.
takeawayTr: Kısa toplar kurulum; winner değildir.
scenarioFr: Tu frappes une balle profonde et ton adversaire répond court au milieu du court. Première décision ?
optionsFr: Avancer, charger ton coup et préparer le +1
Frapper fort pour tenter le gagnant
Jouer prudemment au milieu
explanationFr: Une balle courte n'est pas un coup gagnant : c'est une occasion de transition. Avance, charge, et prépare la balle suivante plutôt que de forcer un gagnant en un coup.
takeawayFr: Les balles courtes sont des préparations, pas des gagnants.

scenario: You've lost serve twice and you're making three unforced errors a game trying to finish rallies from the baseline. Your opponent retrieves everything from a metre behind hers.
options: Aim a metre higher, same pace
Swing harder and end points sooner
Take the pace off and just push
explanation: Raising net clearance a metre cuts errors without changing your game, because the same swing now lands deep instead of in the tape. Swinging harder against a retriever only shrinks the margin that is already failing you.
takeaway: Fix errors with height before you touch your pace.

scenario: In a neutral rally, your opponent's reply lands between the service line and baseline with low spin. What's the trigger?
options: Step in and flatten the ball deep down-the-line or inside-out
Continue the neutral pattern — it's not short enough
Drop shot to shorten the point
explanation: A ball in that zone with low spin is a transition trigger. Flattening with intent pressures the next reply and moves you into position for a +2 finish.
takeaway: Know your attack zone — mid-court with low spin is it.
scenarioTr: Nötr rally'de rakibin yanıtı servis çizgisiyle kalenin arasında, düşük spinle düştü. Tetikleyici ne?
optionsTr: Öne adım at, çizgiye veya inside-out düzleştir
Nötr deseni sürdür — yeterince kısa değil
explanationTr: O bölgedeki düşük spinli top geçiş tetiğidir. Niyetli düzleştirme sonraki yanıtı zorlar ve seni +2 bitirme pozisyonuna taşır.
takeawayTr: Saldırı bölgeni bil — orta kort düşük spinli top orasıdır.
scenarioFr: Dans un échange neutre, sa réponse tombe entre la ligne de service et la ligne de fond, avec peu d'effet. Quel est le déclencheur ?
optionsFr: Avancer et frapper à plat, profond, long de ligne ou décroisé
Continuer le schéma neutre — ce n'est pas assez court
Amortir pour raccourcir le point
explanationFr: Une balle dans cette zone avec peu d'effet est un déclencheur de transition. Frapper à plat avec intention met la réponse suivante sous pression et te place pour conclure au +2.
takeawayFr: Connais ta zone d'attaque : le milieu de court avec peu d'effet, c'est elle.

scenario: 5–5 in the third and the rallies are running past ten balls. You're winning most of them, but you arrive at the ball gasping and your last two forehands sailed long from the middle of the baseline.
options: Breathe out at contact on every ball
Hold it, then breathe once the point ends
Take one deep breath before each serve
explanation: Exhaling on every contact keeps the core stable and stops the oxygen debt that turns long rallies into long errors. Holding it until the point ends is what most club players do, and it is exactly why the tenth ball flies.
takeaway: One exhale per contact, all rally long.

scenario: You've decided to change direction from crosscourt to down-the-line. What's the execution priority?
options: A contact point slightly in front of normal to redirect cleanly
Extra pace to beat the recovery
A higher net clearance
explanation: Direction change requires a slightly earlier contact point to redirect the ball precisely. Pace without precision just sends the ball wide of the line.
takeaway: Direction change is a contact-point problem — not a pace problem.
scenarioTr: Çaprazdan çizgiye yön değiştirmeye karar verdin. Uygulama önceliği ne?
optionsTr: Temiz yönlendirme için normal temas noktasının biraz önünde vur
explanationTr: Yön değişikliği topu hassas yönlendirmek için temas noktasının biraz önde olmasını ister. Hassasiyetsiz hız topu çizgi dışına gönderir.
takeawayTr: Yön değişimi temas noktası meselesidir — hız değil.
scenarioFr: Tu décides de changer de direction, du croisé vers le long de ligne. Quelle est la priorité d'exécution ?
optionsFr: Un point d'impact un peu plus devant que d'habitude pour rediriger proprement
Plus de vitesse pour devancer son replacement
Plus de hauteur au-dessus du filet
explanationFr: Un changement de direction demande un point d'impact légèrement plus tôt pour rediriger la balle précisément. La vitesse sans précision envoie simplement la balle à côté de la ligne.
takeawayFr: Changer de direction est un problème de point d'impact — pas de vitesse.

scenario: You hit a deep slice approach down the line. Where should you be as your opponent makes contact?
options: Inside the service line, split-stepping
Already at the net tape
Behind the baseline still
explanation: Inside the service line with a split step is the textbook position — close enough to cover, balanced enough to react to any pass or lob.
takeaway: Inside the service line, split step — every approach.
scenarioTr: Çizgiye derin slice approach attın. Rakip temas ederken nerede olmalısın?
explanationTr: Servis çizgisinin içinde split step, ders kitabı pozisyonudur — kapsamak için yeterince yakın, her pass veya lop'a tepki için yeterince dengeli.
takeawayTr: Servis çizgisinin içinde split step — her approach'ta.
scenarioFr: Tu montes derrière un slice d'approche profond long de ligne. Où dois-tu être au moment où ton adversaire frappe ?
optionsFr: À l'intérieur de la ligne de service, en split-step
Déjà collé à la bande du filet
Encore derrière la ligne de fond
explanationFr: À l'intérieur de la ligne de service avec un split-step, c'est la position de référence — assez près pour couvrir, assez équilibré pour réagir à un passing ou à un lob.
takeawayFr: À l'intérieur de la ligne de service, split-step — sur chaque montée.

scenario: Opponent shapes to hit a crosscourt passing shot. Where do you volley from?
options: Slightly toward the crosscourt sideline — bisecting the passing lane
Directly on the centre line
Close to the net tape
explanation: Tilting toward the crosscourt side closes the primary passing lane without abandoning the down-the-line. You're defending the likely shot first.
takeaway: Bias your volley position toward the obvious passing lane.
scenarioTr: Rakip çapraz pass atmaya hazırlanıyor. Volley'i nereden alırsın?
optionsTr: Çapraz çizgiye doğru kaydır — pass rotasını ikiye böl
explanationTr: Çapraz tarafa kaymak birincil pass rotasını kapar ama çizgi tarafını terk etmez. Muhtemel atışı önce savunuyorsun.
takeawayTr: Volley pozisyonunu bariz pass rotasına doğru kaydır.
scenarioFr: L'adversaire se prépare à jouer un passing croisé. D'où joues-tu ta volée ?
optionsFr: Légèrement décalé vers le couloir croisé — sur la bissectrice du passing
Exactement sur la ligne médiane
Tout près de la bande du filet
explanationFr: Se décaler du côté croisé ferme le couloir de passing principal sans abandonner le long de ligne. Tu défends d'abord le coup le plus probable.
takeawayFr: Décale ta position de volée vers le passing le plus évident.

focusTag: volley contact on the body ball
scenario: You closed behind an approach and they drive flat at your hip from the baseline. It's 30–30 and your last two body volleys were caught beside you and dumped into the net. Where's the contact?
options: Contact in front of your hip
Block it beside your body
Back up a step to make room
explanation: Contact in front of the lead hip keeps the racket face stable and sends the ball forward, which is how a body ball becomes an attacking volley. Blocking it beside your body gives the racket no room and drops it into the net.
takeaway: Meet body balls in front, never beside you.

scenario: You serve-and-volley and get a low ball at your feet. What's the priority?
options: Scoop it deep down the middle to buy time
Attempt a sharp angle volley winner
Let it bounce and play a groundstroke
explanation: A low first volley is a reset — deep middle buys time to reach the proper volley position for the second volley.
takeaway: First volleys at your feet are setups — not winners.
mistakeType: going for winners on low first volleys
scenarioTr: Servis-volley attın ve ayaklarına düşük top geldi. Öncelik ne?
explanationTr: Düşük ilk volley bir sıfırlamadır — ortadan derine atmak ikinci volley için doğru pozisyona gelme zamanı kazandırır.
takeawayTr: Ayağındaki ilk volley kurulumdur — winner değil.
scenarioFr: Tu sers-volées et tu récupères une balle basse dans les pieds. Quelle est la priorité ?
optionsFr: La relever profond au milieu pour gagner du temps
Tenter une volée d'angle gagnante
La laisser rebondir et jouer un coup de fond
explanationFr: Une première volée basse est une remise en jeu — profond au milieu te donne le temps d'atteindre la bonne position pour la deuxième volée.
takeawayFr: Les premières volées dans les pieds sont des préparations — pas des gagnants.

scenario: Opponent lobs you. Your first movement?
options: Racket up and backpedal laterally in small steps
Sprint straight back with your head down
Watch the ball arc before moving
explanation: Racket-up early and small lateral backpedal steps keep your balance and head position for a clean overhead contact.
takeaway: On a lob: racket up first, feet second.
scenarioTr: Rakip lop attı. İlk hareketin?
optionsTr: Raket yukarıda, küçük yan adımlarla geriye
Topun yörüngesini izle, sonra hareket et
explanationTr: Raketi erken yukarı almak ve küçük yan adımlar dengeyi ve baş pozisyonunu korur — temiz overhead teması için.
takeawayTr: Lop'ta önce raket, sonra ayaklar.
scenarioFr: L'adversaire te lobe. Ton premier mouvement ?
optionsFr: Raquette en haut et petits pas latéraux en reculant
Sprinter en arrière tête baissée
Regarder la trajectoire avant de bouger
explanationFr: Raquette levée tôt et petits pas latéraux en recul gardent ton équilibre et la position de ta tête pour une smash propre.
takeawayFr: Sur un lob : la raquette d'abord, les pieds ensuite.

scenario: A high floating ball comes to you at the service line with your opponent deep behind the baseline. Choice?
options: Angled deep volley to keep them pinned back
A drop volley short crosscourt
A full-pace volley down the middle
explanation: When the opponent is deep, a deep angled volley maintains the advantage. A drop volley brings them into play — risky when they're already out of position.
takeaway: When opponents are deep, keep them deep — don't invite them in.
scenarioTr: Yüksek havada top servis çizgisine geliyor, rakip kalenin derinlerinde. Seçim?
optionsTr: Derin açılı volley — onları geride tut
explanationTr: Rakip geride olduğunda derin açılı volley avantajı sürdürür. Drop volley onları oyuna çeker — zaten pozisyon dışıysa risk.
takeawayTr: Rakip geridelerse geride tut — içeri davet etme.
scenarioFr: Une balle haute et flottante arrive sur toi à la ligne de service, ton adversaire est loin derrière sa ligne de fond. Ton choix ?
optionsFr: Une volée profonde et angulée pour le garder au fond
Une volée amortie courte croisée
Une volée pleine vitesse au milieu
explanationFr: Quand l'adversaire est loin, une volée profonde et angulée conserve l'avantage. Une volée amortie le fait entrer dans le court — risqué alors qu'il est déjà mal placé.
takeawayFr: Quand ils sont loin, garde-les loin — ne les invite pas.

focusTag: swing length on a hard pass
scenario: You poached and they answer with a hard flat pass at your chest from the service line. It's 30–40 and you've swung at the last two of these and flown both long.
options: Block it short and firm, no backswing
Take a full swing and try to end it
Soften the hands and slice it back
explanation: Their pace is already on the ball, so a short firm block redirects it and keeps the strings behind the shot. A full swing adds speed you do not need and is precisely what sent the last two long.
takeaway: Hard ball at you: block it, don't swing at it.

scenario: A hard ball dips to your feet at the transition zone. What's the right play?
options: A soft half-volley deep to the middle
A hard half-volley trying to punch a winner
Let it bounce and scramble
explanation: A soft half-volley uses the opponent's pace, clears the net, and buys time. A hard one usually sprays. Letting it bounce means you're on the baseline without having gained anything.
takeaway: Half-volleys are survival shots — soft, deep, and middle.
scenarioTr: Geçiş bölgesinde ayağına sert dip top geliyor. Doğru oyun?
explanationTr: Yumuşak half-volley rakibin hızını kullanır, fileyi geçer ve zaman kazandırır. Sert olan çoğu zaman savrulur.
takeawayTr: Half-volley bir hayatta kalma vuruşudur — yumuşak, derin, orta.
scenarioFr: Une balle rapide plonge dans tes pieds dans la zone de transition. Quel est le bon coup ?
optionsFr: Une demi-volée douce, profonde au milieu
Une demi-volée frappée fort pour tenter le gagnant
La laisser rebondir et courir
explanationFr: Une demi-volée douce utilise la vitesse adverse, passe le filet et gagne du temps. Frappée fort, elle part généralement dehors. La laisser rebondir te ramène à la ligne de fond sans rien avoir gagné.
takeawayFr: Les demi-volées sont des coups de survie — douces, profondes, au milieu.

focusTag: overhead timing on a short lob
scenario: 40–30, you've closed to two metres from the net and they scramble up a floating lob dropping around your service line. There is no wind and the sun is behind you.
options: Cross-step back and take it in the air
Let it bounce first, then hit the overhead
Drop back and play it off the ground
explanation: A short floating lob in still air is a free smash, and taking it in the air keeps them scrambling instead of giving them two seconds back. Letting it bounce is right only on a deep heavy lob you cannot reach in balance.
takeaway: Short lob, hit it in the air; deep lob, let it bounce.

scenario: You're at the net and your opponent is recovering from wide in the deuce court. Best volley target?
options: Open ad court — deep into the corner
Behind them back into the deuce corner
Short drop volley
explanation: Opponent recovering means they're moving toward the centre. Deep into the open ad court makes them reverse direction and arrive off-balance — or not at all.
takeaway: At the net, hit away from their recovery — not back to where they came from.
scenarioTr: File önündesin ve rakip deuce tarafta açıktan toparlanıyor. En iyi volley hedefi?
explanationTr: Toparlanan rakip ortaya doğru hareket eder. Açık ad köşesine derin volley yön değiştirmeye zorlar ve dengesiz yakalar — ya da hiç yetişemez.
takeawayTr: File önünde toparlanma yönünün tersine vur — geldiği yere değil.
scenarioFr: Tu es au filet et ton adversaire revient d'une position très excentrée côté égalité. Meilleure cible de volée ?
optionsFr: Le côté avantage libre — profond dans le coin
Derrière lui, de nouveau dans le coin égalité
Une volée amortie courte
explanationFr: S'il se replace, il se déplace vers le centre. Profond dans le côté avantage libre l'oblige à repartir en sens inverse et à arriver en déséquilibre — ou à ne pas arriver du tout.
takeawayFr: Au filet, joue à l'opposé de son replacement — pas là d'où il vient.

focusTag: carrying a set into the next
scenario: You lost the first set 6–4 and three of those games ended with a double fault at deuce. You serve first in the second set against a returner standing two metres back.
options: Set one intention: full kick second serve to the backhand
Set a score goal: win the first three games of the set
Replay the double faults to find the toss problem
explanation: A lost set is only useful once it becomes one thing you will do, and a committed kick to the backhand attacks the exact game that broke you. The score goal of three games targets what you cannot control and rebuilds the same deuce tension.
takeaway: Turn a lost set into one thing you will do.

scenario: Serving at 30–30, your clean winner is called out and you saw the mark land in. Your opponent has already turned and is waiting to receive the next point.
options: Take the full time at the towel, then serve your usual pattern
Go straight back and serve flat and big while you are fired up
Play the next two points safe until the anger passes
explanation: The towel walk spends the adrenaline before it reaches your racquet and keeps your 30–30 serve pattern intact. Serving big while fired up feels like justice, but arousal that high shortens the swing and gives away the game instead.
takeaway: One bad call costs one point, not two.
mistakeType: playing angry after a bad call

scenario: Tiebreak at 3–4 and you have just missed the first serve. Both of your double faults today came on second serves you flattened out under pressure.
options: Hit your normal kick second serve to the backhand
Push it in softly and start the rally from behind
Flatten it out so the return cannot be attacked
explanation: Breakers are decided by the points you hand over, and your practised kick neither double faults nor invites a free swing. Pushing it in softly avoids the fault but donates the mini-break on the return one shot later.
takeaway: In a breaker, serve the second serve you practise.

scenario: Break point down at 30–40, you step in on a mid-court forehand. Your last two forehands from that spot flew long and the words in your head are ‘don’t miss’.
options: Pick a target: crosscourt, two metres inside the baseline
Cue the technique: finish the swing over your shoulder
Take the pace off and roll it deep to the middle
explanation: An external target gives attention one job and lets a rehearsed swing run itself on the shot you just missed twice. The technique cue turns the stroke into a thought under pressure, which is what sent those two forehands long.
takeaway: Aim at a spot, not at your swing.

scenario: Your opponent bounces once and serves within eight seconds, and you have lost three straight return games playing at that speed. You are 1–4 down, walking in to receive.
options: Stay at the back fence and take your own full time
Match their tempo to keep them from settling in
Return from a step further back to buy yourself time
explanation: The receiver decides when play starts, so taking your full time rebuilds the routine you have gone three return games without. Matching their tempo keeps you inside their rhythm and leaves you choosing a return target after the toss.
takeaway: The receiver owns the clock — use it.

scenario: Your opponent has won four games in a row, jogs between points and serves within ten seconds. You are 2–5 down and about to serve.
options: Use your full time between points and towel at the change
Start the game quickly before they settle into it
Switch to a different style for a couple of games
explanation: A streak runs on tempo, and taking your full time leaves them standing still with a lead to think about. Starting quickly to catch them cold keeps the match at the speed that just produced four straight games.
takeaway: Cool a hot streak by slowing the clock.

scenario: You were broken serving for the match at 5–4 and they now serve at 5–5. They have missed the first serve on six of the last eight points.
options: Step in on their second serve early in the game
Extend the rallies and let the pressure work on them
Go big on the first return to break straight back
explanation: They are serving their tightest game of the match, so standing in on that second serve converts their dropping first-serve rate into pressure immediately. Extending rallies gives them time to settle and hands back the discomfort.
takeaway: They serve scared too — stand in and take it.

scenario: You have lost five of the last six games. The one thing still working is the kick serve to the ad-court backhand: eight of nine points won behind it today.
options: Start every service point with that kick serve
Serve and volley to shorten the points instead
Grind long rallies until the ball feels clean
explanation: Confidence comes back from points won, and the serve already producing eight of nine is the cheapest source of them. Serving and volleying to shorten points adds an unrehearsed skill at the moment your margin is smallest.
takeaway: Lean on what is already winning points.

scenario: You lost 6–4, 6–4 to a player you had beaten twice before. Driving home, you can still see the three volleys you missed at 4–4 in the second set.
options: Write two things that worked and one fix, tonight
List every error you made while it is still fresh
Head to the practice court tomorrow and drill volleys
explanation: Two-plus-one keeps the review short enough to stay accurate and leaves practice with one clear job. Listing every error while it is fresh is rumination with a notebook, and it teaches your memory that the match was only misses.
takeaway: Two things that worked, one to fix — then stop.

scenario: First time against this opponent and five minutes of warm-up remain. You have rallied from the baseline but have not yet seen their backhand or their second serve.
options: Feed a few balls to each wing and watch which one floats
Groove your own forehand until the contact feels clean
Hit at half pace and save your legs for the match
explanation: The warm-up is the only free scouting you get, and knowing which wing floats decides your first three service patterns. Grooving your own forehand feels productive but walks you to the first point with no plan for where the ball goes.
takeaway: Warm up your plan, not only your strokes.

scenario: You and your partner are one-up-one-back. Your baseline partner gets a short, floaty ball mid-court. What should you both do?
options: Both move up to the net together behind the approach
Stay put — keep one player back to cover
Partner hits it and retreats to the baseline
explanation: A short ball is your cue to get BOTH players to the net. The both-up formation wins the majority of club points, so your partner approaches and joins you.
takeaway: Short ball = both up. The team that reaches the net first usually wins the point.
scenarioTr: Sen ve partnerin biri-önde-biri-arkada dizilimindesiniz. Arkadaki partnerin kısa, yumuşak bir top alıyor. İkiniz ne yapmalısınız?
optionsTr: İkiniz birlikte file'ye çıkın (yaklaşma vuruşunun arkasından)
Olduğunuz yerde kalın — biriniz arkada kalsın
explanationTr: Kısa top, ikinizi de file'ye çıkarma işaretidir. Her ikisi de file'de (both-up) dizilimi kulüp puanlarının çoğunu kazanır; partnerin yaklaşıp sana katılır.
takeawayTr: Kısa top = ikiniz de file'ye. File'ye önce ulaşan takım genelde puanı alır.
scenarioFr: Ton partenaire et toi êtes un devant, un derrière. Ton partenaire de fond récupère une balle courte et flottante au milieu du court. Que faites-vous ?
optionsFr: Monter tous les deux au filet derrière l'approche
Ne rien changer — garder un joueur derrière pour couvrir
Il frappe et retourne à la ligne de fond
explanationFr: Une balle courte, c'est le signal pour amener les DEUX joueurs au filet. La formation deux-devant gagne la majorité des points en club : ton partenaire monte et te rejoint.
takeawayFr: Balle courte = les deux devant. L'équipe qui arrive au filet la première gagne généralement le point.

scenario: You're the net player while your partner serves. Where should you start to begin the point?
options: Centred, ready to poach the middle
Tight to your alley to protect the line
Back near the service line, playing it safe
explanation: Start central and look to poach the middle — most balls travel through the middle, and guarding the alley gives away the bigger target. Cover the alley only on an obviously wide ball.
takeaway: The net player's #1 job is the middle, not the alley.
mistakeType: net player glued to the alley
scenarioTr: Partnerin servis atarken sen file oyuncususun. Puana başlamak için nerede durmalısın?
explanationTr: Ortada başla ve ortadan poach'a bak — topların çoğu ortadan gelir; koridoru korumak daha büyük hedefi açık bırakır. Koridoru sadece bariz geniş topta kapat.
takeawayTr: File oyuncusunun bir numaralı işi orta, koridor değil.
scenarioFr: Tu es au filet pendant que ton partenaire sert. Où te places-tu au début du point ?
optionsFr: Au centre, prêt à intercepter au milieu
Collé à ton couloir pour protéger la ligne
En retrait près de la ligne de service, par sécurité
explanationFr: Pars au centre et cherche à intercepter au milieu — la plupart des balles passent par là, et garder le couloir donne la plus grande cible à l'adversaire. Ne couvre le couloir que sur une balle clairement extérieure.
takeawayFr: La mission numéro 1 du joueur de filet, c'est le milieu, pas le couloir.

scenario: You're serving and volleying. The return comes back LOW at your feet. Where do you place the first volley?
options: Deep to the baseline returner, or low through the middle
Hard at the opposing net player
A soft drop into their service box
explanation: On a low/defensive ball, don't reflexively aim at the net player — a low volley there is an easy put-away for them. Go deep to the baseliner or low through the middle and keep climbing to the net.
takeaway: First-volley target depends on height: a low ball goes deep/middle, not at the net player.
mistakeType: first volley auto-aimed at the net player
scenarioTr: Servis-vole oynuyorsun. Karşılama ayaklarına ALÇAK geliyor. İlk voleyi nereye koyarsın?
optionsTr: Derine, baseline'daki returner'a — ya da alçak, ortadan
explanationTr: Alçak/defansif topta refleksle file oyuncusuna vurma — oradaki alçak vole onlara kolay sayı olur. Derine baseliner'a ya da alçak ortadan oyna ve file'ye çıkmaya devam et.
takeawayTr: İlk vole hedefi yüksekliğe bağlı: alçak top derine/ortaya gider, file oyuncusuna değil.
scenarioFr: Tu sers-volées. Le retour revient BAS dans tes pieds. Où places-tu ta première volée ?
optionsFr: Profond sur le relanceur au fond, ou bas par le milieu
Fort sur le joueur adverse au filet
Une amortie douce dans son carré de service
explanationFr: Sur une balle basse et défensive, ne vise pas par réflexe le joueur au filet — une volée basse là-bas est un cadeau à smasher. Joue profond sur le joueur de fond ou bas par le milieu, et continue d'avancer au filet.
takeawayFr: La cible de la première volée dépend de la hauteur : une balle basse part profond ou au milieu, pas sur le joueur au filet.

scenario: You're returning serve in doubles against a team with one player at the net. What's the priority on your return?
options: Keep it LOW, cross-court at the volleyer's feet
Drive it deep and flat down the middle
Loop it high cross-court for safety
explanation: A low cross-court return at the incoming volleyer's feet is the hardest ball to attack. A floaty/high return is poach bait. Your goal is to get your team forward, not to win it outright.
takeaway: Doubles return = low at the volleyer's feet. Floaters get poached.
scenarioTr: Biri file'de olan bir takıma karşı çiftlerde karşılama yapıyorsun. Karşılamada öncelik ne?
optionsTr: ALÇAK tut, çaprazda voleyi yapanın ayaklarına
Güvenli olsun diye yükseğe, çaprazda lob gibi
explanationTr: Voleye gelenin ayaklarına alçak çapraz karşılama, saldırması en zor toptur. Yüksek/yumuşak karşılama poach yemidir. Amaç puanı tek vuruşta bitirmek değil, takımını öne taşımak.
takeawayTr: Çiftlerde karşılama = voleyi yapanın ayaklarına alçak. Yumuşak toplar poach yer.
scenarioFr: Tu retournes en double contre une équipe avec un joueur au filet. Quelle est la priorité sur ton retour ?
optionsFr: Le garder BAS, croisé, dans les pieds du volleyeur
Le frapper profond et à plat au milieu
Le lifter haut en croisé, par sécurité
explanationFr: Un retour bas et croisé dans les pieds du volleyeur qui monte est la balle la plus difficile à attaquer. Un retour haut et flottant se fait intercepter. Ton but est de faire avancer ton équipe, pas de gagner le point d'un coup.
takeawayFr: Retour en double = bas, dans les pieds du volleyeur. Les balles flottantes se font intercepter.

scenario: You decide to poach. When exactly do you commit to crossing?
options: Just after the serve bounces, as the returner starts the forward swing
The instant your partner tosses to serve
After the return has already cleared the net
explanation: Commit just after the serve bounces, as the returner starts their forward swing — early enough to cross and cut off the middle, late enough that they can't redirect the ball behind you.
takeaway: Poach as the returner starts the swing — not too early, not too late.
scenarioTr: Poach yapmaya karar verdin. Tam olarak ne zaman çıkarsın?
optionsTr: Servis sektikten hemen sonra, returner ileri vuruşa başlarken
explanationTr: Servis sektikten hemen sonra, returner ileri vuruşa başlarken çık — ortayı kesmek için yeterince erken, arkana yönlendirilemeyecek kadar geç.
takeawayTr: Returner vuruşa başlarken poach yap — ne çok erken, ne çok geç.
scenarioFr: Tu décides d'intercepter. À quel moment exactement t'engages-tu ?
optionsFr: Juste après le rebond du service, quand le relanceur amorce son geste vers l'avant
À l'instant où ton partenaire lance sa balle de service
Une fois que le retour a déjà passé le filet
explanationFr: Engage-toi juste après le rebond du service, quand le relanceur amorce son geste — assez tôt pour traverser et couper le milieu, assez tard pour qu'il ne puisse plus rediriger derrière toi.
takeawayFr: Intercepte quand le relanceur amorce son geste — ni trop tôt, ni trop tard.

scenario: The opponents lob over your partner's head to the open side. Who takes the ball, and what do you call?
options: You (the un-lobbed player) call 'switch' and cross to cover
Your partner sprints back to chase their own side
Both of you retreat to the baseline and reset
explanation: On a lob over one player, the UN-lobbed partner calls 'switch' and crosses to cover the open side, while the lobbed player rotates across to the other side. Rotating as a unit beats both scrambling backward.
takeaway: Lobbed over your partner? You call 'switch' and cross. Move as a unit.
scenarioTr: Rakip, partnerinin kafasından açık tarafa lob attı. Topu kim alır ve sen ne dersin?
optionsTr: Sen (lob yemeyen oyuncu) 'switch' deyip çapraz geçip kapatırsın
Partnerin kendi tarafını kovalamak için geri koşar
explanationTr: Bir oyuncunun üstünden lob gelince, lob YEMEYEN partner 'switch' der ve açık tarafı kapatmak için çapraz geçer; lob yiyen oyuncu diğer tarafa döner. Birim olarak dönmek, ikinizin de geri savrulmasından iyidir.
takeawayTr: Partnerinin üstünden lob mu? Sen 'switch' deyip çapraz geç. Birim gibi hareket et.
scenarioFr: Les adversaires lobent au-dessus de ton partenaire, du côté libre. Qui prend la balle et qu'annonces-tu ?
optionsFr: Toi (le joueur non lobé) : tu annonces « switch » et tu traverses
Ton partenaire sprinte en arrière pour chasser son côté
Vous reculez tous les deux à la ligne de fond
explanationFr: Sur un lob au-dessus d'un joueur, c'est le partenaire NON lobé qui annonce « switch » et traverse pour couvrir le côté libre, pendant que le joueur lobé bascule de l'autre côté. Tourner en bloc vaut mieux que deux joueurs qui reculent chacun de leur côté.
takeawayFr: Lob au-dessus de ton partenaire ? Tu annonces « switch » et tu traverses. Déplacez-vous en bloc.

scenario: Your partner is at the net ready to poach. Where should you serve to set them up?
options: To the body or the T, pulling the return toward the middle
Wide, to open the angle for yourself
A soft, high serve to start the point safely
explanation: A serve to the body or the T pulls the return toward the middle — exactly where your net partner can poach. A wide serve opens angles AWAY from your poacher. Keep your first-serve percentage high too.
takeaway: Serve body/T to feed your partner's poach; protect first-serve %.
mistakeType: serve placement that doesn't set up the partner
scenarioTr: Partnerin file'de poach'a hazır. Onu kurmak için nereye servis atmalısın?
optionsTr: Vücuda ya da T'ye — karşılamayı ortaya çeker
Puana güvenli başlamak için yumuşak, yüksek servis
explanationTr: Vücuda ya da T'ye servis, karşılamayı ortaya çeker — tam da file partnerinin poach yapabileceği yere. Geniş servis ise açıları poach'çından UZAĞA açar. İlk servis yüzdeni de yüksek tut.
takeawayTr: Partnerinin poach'ını beslemek için vücuda/T'ye servis at; ilk servis yüzdeni koru.
scenarioFr: Ton partenaire est au filet, prêt à intercepter. Où sers-tu pour le mettre en position ?
optionsFr: Sur le corps ou au T, pour ramener le retour vers le milieu
Extérieur, pour t'ouvrir l'angle à toi
Un service haut et lent pour démarrer le point tranquillement
explanationFr: Un service sur le corps ou au T ramène le retour vers le milieu — exactement là où ton partenaire peut intercepter. Un service extérieur ouvre les angles À L'OPPOSÉ de ton intercepteur. Garde aussi un bon pourcentage de premières balles.
takeawayFr: Sers corps/T pour nourrir l'interception de ton partenaire ; protège ton pourcentage de premières balles.

scenario: A ball comes right down the middle between you and your partner. Who should take it?
options: The pre-agreed player — by default, the one whose forehand is in the middle
Whoever happens to be closer in that instant
Both go for it, to be safe
explanation: 'Down the middle solves the riddle.' Pre-decide who takes the middle (default: the forehand player) so two racquets don't collide or both leave it. Decide before the point, not during it.
takeaway: Pre-assign the middle to the forehand player. Don't decide mid-point.
scenarioTr: Top, sen ve partnerinin tam ortasından geliyor. Kim almalı?
optionsTr: Önceden anlaşılan oyuncu — varsayılan olarak forehand'i ortada olan
explanationTr: 'Down the middle solves the riddle.' Ortayı kimin alacağını önceden belirle (varsayılan: forehand oyuncusu) ki iki raket çarpışmasın ya da ikisi de bırakmasın. Puan sırasında değil, öncesinde karar ver.
takeawayTr: Ortayı önceden forehand oyuncusuna ata. Puan ortasında karar verme.
scenarioFr: Une balle arrive pile au milieu, entre ton partenaire et toi. Qui la prend ?
optionsFr: Le joueur convenu à l'avance — par défaut, celui dont le coup droit est au milieu
Celui qui se trouve le plus près à cet instant
Les deux, par sécurité
explanationFr: « Au milieu, on résout l'énigme. » Décidez à l'avance qui prend le milieu (par défaut : le joueur en coup droit) pour éviter que deux raquettes se percutent ou que personne n'y aille. Ça se décide avant le point, pas pendant.
takeawayFr: Attribue le milieu au joueur en coup droit à l'avance. Ne décide pas en plein point.

scenario: A big server is crushing your partner's return and picking off your net player. What formation adjustment helps?
options: Both go back for a game, then work forward again
Keep one up and shorten your partner's return swing
Both move up to take the return early
explanation: Both-back absorbs a serve your partner cannot block from a normal return position, and it is temporary — you climb back once a return lands deep. Keeping one up only asks the same net player to survive the same ball again.
takeaway: Both-back is a shield you raise, not a formation you live in.
mistakeType: leaving the net player exposed to a big serve

scenario: The opposing net player keeps poaching and crowding the middle, eating your returns. How do you make them pay?
options: Lob the aggressive net player to push them off the net
Hit harder cross-court through the same spot
Aim every return down their alley
explanation: A lob over the crowding net player resets the point and pushes them off the net, making them respect the lob and poach less. Hitting harder into the poach is exactly what they want.
takeaway: Punish an over-eager poacher with a lob — it buys back the middle.
scenarioTr: Karşı file oyuncusu sürekli poach yapıp ortayı daraltıyor, karşılamalarını yiyor. Bedelini nasıl ödetirsin?
optionsTr: Agresif file oyuncusunu lob'la, file'den uzaklaştır
Aynı noktadan daha sert çapraz vur
explanationTr: Ortayı daraltan file oyuncusunun üstünden lob, puanı sıfırlar ve onu file'den uzaklaştırır; lob'a saygı duyup daha az poach yapar. Poach'ın içine daha sert vurmak tam da onların istediğidir.
takeawayTr: Fazla hevesli bir poach'çıyı lob'la cezalandır — ortayı geri kazandırır.
scenarioFr: Le joueur adverse au filet intercepte sans arrêt et mange tes retours au milieu. Comment le faire payer ?
optionsFr: Lober le joueur de filet agressif pour le repousser
Frapper plus fort en croisé au même endroit
Viser son couloir à chaque retour
explanationFr: Un lob au-dessus du joueur qui s'avance remet le point à zéro et le repousse du filet : il devra respecter le lob et interceptera moins. Frapper plus fort dans son interception, c'est exactement ce qu'il attend.
takeawayFr: Punis un intercepteur trop gourmand avec un lob — ça te rend le milieu.

scenario: Deuce court, 30-30. You've noticed the returner chips a short, floaty backhand every time you serve into their body. What's the highest-value play?
options: Serve the body again, then step in and take the short chip early with a forehand
Go for a flat ace down the T
Serve wide to their forehand to open the court
explanation: You've read a reliable tendency. The body serve jams the backhand and forces the short floater — so trigger it on purpose, anticipate the reply, move in, and attack it on the rise. You're hunting the +1, not the ace.
takeaway: When you've read a return tendency, serve to trigger it — then pounce on the predictable reply.
mistakeType: ignoring a read for a low-percentage ace
scenarioTr: Deuce bölgesi, 30-30. Rakip, gövdesine servis attığında her seferinde kısa, yumuşak bir backhand chip atıyor. En değerli oyun ne?
optionsTr: Tekrar gövdeye servis at, sonra öne çıkıp kısa chip'i forehand'le erken al
Forehand'ine açık servis atıp sahayı aç
explanationTr: Güvenilir bir eğilim okudun. Gövde servisi backhand'i sıkıştırıp kısa topu zorluyor — o yüzden bilerek tetikle, cevabı önceden kestir, öne çık ve topu yükselirken vur. As değil, +1 peşindesin.
takeawayTr: Bir karşılama eğilimi okuduysan, onu tetikleyecek servisi at — sonra tahmin edilebilir cevabın üstüne çök.
scenarioFr: Côté égalité, 30-30. Tu as remarqué que le relanceur chippe un revers court et flottant à chaque fois que tu sers sur son corps. Quel est le coup le plus rentable ?
optionsFr: Resservir sur le corps, puis avancer et attaquer tôt le chip court en coup droit
Tenter un ace à plat au T
Servir extérieur sur son coup droit pour ouvrir le court
explanationFr: Tu as lu une tendance fiable. Le service sur le corps coince le revers et provoque la balle courte et flottante : déclenche-la exprès, anticipe la réponse, avance et attaque à la montée. Tu chasses le +1, pas l'ace.
takeawayFr: Quand tu as lu une tendance de retour, sers pour la déclencher — puis fonds sur la réponse prévisible.

scenario: 4-5 down, 0-30 on the return, fast court, against a big server who goes 70% to your backhand. Where do you stand and what's the goal?
options: Shade a half-step toward the backhand and block deep down the middle
Hold your normal spot and try to rip a clean winner
Back up two metres and slice every return
explanation: Against a bomb on a fast court the realistic goal is a neutral return, not a winner. Shade toward the 70% target, shorten to a block, and aim deep down the middle — it cuts the server's next angle and buys time to recover.
takeaway: Vs a big server: shade to the pattern, block deep middle, accept neutral — survive before you attack.
mistakeType: going for a winner off an unreturnable serve
scenarioTr: 4-5 geride, karşılamada 0-30, hızlı kort, backhand'ine %70 giden güçlü bir servisçiye karşı. Nerede durursun, hedefin ne?
optionsTr: Yarım adım backhand'e kay ve ortadan derin blokla
Normal yerinde dur ve temiz bir winner vurmaya çalış
İki metre geri çekil ve her karşılamayı slice'la
explanationTr: Hızlı kortta bomba servise karşı gerçekçi hedef winner değil, nötr bir karşılamadır. %70'lik hedefe doğru kay, vuruşu kısaltıp blokla ve ortadan derin at — bu, servisçinin bir sonraki açısını keser ve toparlanmana zaman kazandırır.
takeawayTr: Güçlü servisçiye karşı: desene göre kay, ortadan derin blokla, nötrü kabul et — saldırmadan önce hayatta kal.
scenarioFr: Mené 4-5, 0-30 sur son service, court rapide, face à un gros serveur qui va 70 % sur ton revers. Où te places-tu et quel est l'objectif ?
optionsFr: Te décaler d'un demi-pas vers le revers et bloquer profond au milieu
Rester à ta place habituelle et tenter un gagnant propre
Reculer de deux mètres et slicer chaque retour
explanationFr: Face à une bombe sur court rapide, l'objectif réaliste est un retour neutre, pas un gagnant. Décale-toi vers la cible à 70 %, raccourcis en bloc et vise profond au milieu — ça coupe l'angle du coup suivant et te laisse le temps de te replacer.
takeawayFr: Contre un gros serveur : décale-toi vers son schéma, bloque profond au milieu, accepte le neutre — survivre avant d'attaquer.

scenario: A long crosscourt forehand exchange, both deep. Your opponent's crosscourt is landing a little shorter each ball. What's the highest-percentage way to change the pattern?
options: Wait for the short ball, step in, and go inside-out forehand to their backhand
Rip it down the line off the next deep ball
Keep grinding the same crosscourt and wait for the error
explanation: The shortening ball is your cue. Changing direction off a deep ball is low-percentage — instead, wait for the short one, step in, and flip the diagonal inside-out to their backhand. You change the pattern from strength, not desperation.
takeaway: Change direction off the SHORT ball, not the deep one — let the rally hand you the opening.
mistakeType: changing direction off a deep defensive ball
scenarioTr: Uzun bir çapraz forehand alışverişi, ikiniz de derindesiniz. Rakibin çaprazı her topta biraz daha kısa düşüyor. Deseni değiştirmenin en yüksek ihtimalli yolu ne?
optionsTr: Kısa topu bekle, öne çık ve içeriden-dışarı (inside-out) forehand'le backhand'ine at
Bir sonraki derin topta çizgiye sert vur
Aynı çaprazı öğütmeye devam edip hatayı bekle
explanationTr: Kısalan top senin işaretin. Derin toptan yön değiştirmek düşük ihtimallidir — bunun yerine kısa topu bekle, öne çık ve çaprazı inside-out backhand'ine çevir. Deseni çaresizlikten değil, güçten değiştirirsin.
takeawayTr: Yönü KISA toptan değiştir, derinden değil — açığı rallinin sana vermesine izin ver.
scenarioFr: Long échange de coups droits croisés, tous les deux au fond. Son croisé tombe un peu plus court à chaque balle. Quelle est la façon la plus rentable de changer le schéma ?
optionsFr: Attendre la balle courte, avancer et jouer un coup droit décroisé sur son revers
Frapper long de ligne sur la prochaine balle profonde
Continuer à user le même croisé et attendre la faute
explanationFr: La balle qui raccourcit est ton signal. Changer de direction sur une balle profonde est peu rentable — attends la balle courte, avance et inverse la diagonale en décroisé sur son revers. Tu changes le schéma en position de force, pas de désespoir.
takeawayFr: Change de direction sur la balle COURTE, pas sur la profonde — laisse l'échange t'offrir l'ouverture.

scenario: You approached down the line and you're at the service line — not yet at the net — as your opponent loads up for a crosscourt pass. What's the play?
options: Split-step, cover the crosscourt, and punch the volley deep behind them
Sprint all the way to the net and guess a side
Retreat to the baseline to retrieve the pass
explanation: From the service line you can't angle a volley safely. Your DTL approach already closed the line, so split-step, cover the higher-percentage crosscourt pass, and punch the volley DEEP behind the moving opponent — depth over a risky angle from too far back.
takeaway: Caught at the service line: split, cover the crosscourt, volley deep behind them — not a fancy angle.
mistakeType: attempting an angled volley from too far back
scenarioTr: Çizgi boyunca (down-the-line) yaklaştın ve servis çizgisindesin — henüz file'de değil — rakip çapraz geçiş için hazırlanırken. Oyun ne?
optionsTr: Split-step at, çaprazı kapat ve voleyi onların arkasına derin vur
File'ye kadar koş ve bir tarafı tahmin et
Geçişi almak için baseline'a geri çekil
explanationTr: Servis çizgisinden voleyi güvenle açılandıramazsın. DTL yaklaşman çizgiyi zaten kapattı; o yüzden split-step at, daha yüksek ihtimalli çapraz geçişi kapat ve voleyi hareket eden rakibin arkasına DERİN vur — çok geriden riskli bir açı yerine derinlik.
takeawayTr: Servis çizgisinde yakalandın: split at, çaprazı kapat, voleyi onların arkasına derin vur — süslü açı değil.
scenarioFr: Tu as monté long de ligne et tu es à la ligne de service — pas encore au filet — quand ton adversaire arme un passing croisé. Que fais-tu ?
optionsFr: Split-step, couvrir le croisé et pousser la volée profond derrière lui
Sprinter jusqu'au filet et deviner un côté
Reculer à la ligne de fond pour récupérer le passing
explanationFr: Depuis la ligne de service, tu ne peux pas angler une volée sans risque. Ton approche long de ligne a déjà fermé la ligne : split-step, couvre le passing croisé le plus probable, et pousse la volée PROFOND derrière l'adversaire lancé — la profondeur plutôt qu'un angle risqué de trop loin.
takeawayFr: Coincé à la ligne de service : split, couvre le croisé, volée profonde derrière lui — pas d'angle sophistiqué.

scenario: You served for the set at 5-3 and got broken to 5-4 after two double faults. What's the reset for the next game?
options: Lengthen your between-point routine and recommit to a high-percentage target
Go for broke immediately to win the break back
Replay the double faults in your head to fix the toss
explanation: After a choke-break the fix is process, not panic. Slow your tempo between points, breathe, and reset to a bigger target (margin over the lines). Don't chase the break back recklessly or ruminate on the misses — play the next point on its own merits.
takeaway: After a choke: slow the tempo, widen your margins, play the next point — don't chase or ruminate.
mistakeType: panicking or ruminating after a costly game
scenarioTr: 5-3'te set için servis attın ve iki çift hatadan sonra 5-4'e break yedin. Bir sonraki oyun için reset ne?
optionsTr: Puanlar arası rutinini uzat ve yüksek ihtimalli bir hedefe yeniden bağlan
Break'i hemen geri almak için her şeyi göze al
Servisini düzeltmek için çift hataları kafanda tekrar oynat
explanationTr: Choke-break'ten sonra çözüm panik değil, süreçtir. Puanlar arası temponu yavaşlat, nefes al ve daha büyük bir hedefe (çizgilerden pay) dön. Break'i pervasızca kovalama ya da kaçırdıklarını kafanda evirip çevirme — bir sonraki puanı kendi başına oyna.
takeawayTr: Choke'tan sonra: tempoyu yavaşlat, paylarını genişlet, bir sonraki puanı oyna — kovalama ya da geviş getirme.
scenarioFr: Tu servais pour le set à 5-3 et tu t'es fait breaker à 5-4 après deux doubles fautes. Comment repartir au jeu suivant ?
optionsFr: Allonger ta routine entre les points et te réengager sur une cible à haut pourcentage
Tout tenter immédiatement pour re-breaker
Repasser les doubles fautes en tête pour corriger le lancer
explanationFr: Après un break subi sous pression, la solution est le processus, pas la panique. Ralentis ton tempo entre les points, respire, et reviens à une cible plus large (de la marge sur les lignes). Ne cours pas après le re-break et ne rumine pas — joue le point suivant pour lui-même.
takeawayFr: Après un craquage : ralentis le tempo, élargis tes marges, joue le point suivant — ne cours pas après, ne rumine pas.

scenario: You're serving in doubles, partner at the net. The returner has burned your partner twice with crosscourt returns dipping at their feet. Best adjustment?
options: Switch to I-formation (or fake a poach) to scramble the returner's target
Tell your partner to back off toward the service line
Just serve harder up the T every time
explanation: The returner has a comfortable, grooved target — crosscourt at the net player's feet. Take it away by hiding where the net player will be: I-formation or a fake poach forces the returner to decide late and abandon a pattern that's been working.
takeaway: When a returner grooves a target, hide your net player — I-formation or a fake resets their decision.
mistakeType: staying predictable against a hot returner
scenarioTr: Doubles'ta servis atıyorsun, partnerin file'de. Karşılayan, partnerini iki kez ayaklarına düşen çapraz karşılamalarla yaktı. En iyi ayar ne?
optionsTr: I-formation'a geç (ya da sahte poach yap) ve karşılayanın hedefini boz
Partnerine servis çizgisine doğru geri çekilmesini söyle
Sadece her seferinde T'den daha sert servis at
explanationTr: Karşılayanın rahat, oturmuş bir hedefi var — file oyuncusunun ayaklarına çapraz. File oyuncusunun nerede olacağını gizleyerek bunu elinden al: I-formation ya da sahte poach, karşılayanı geç karar vermeye ve işe yarayan deseni bırakmaya zorlar.
takeawayTr: Karşılayan bir hedefi oturttuysa file oyuncunu gizle — I-formation ya da sahte hamle kararını sıfırlar.
scenarioFr: Tu sers en double, ton partenaire au filet. Le relanceur l'a déjà brûlé deux fois avec des retours croisés qui plongent dans ses pieds. Meilleur ajustement ?
optionsFr: Passer en formation en I (ou simuler une interception) pour brouiller sa cible
Dire à ton partenaire de reculer vers la ligne de service
Servir simplement plus fort au T à chaque fois
explanationFr: Le relanceur a une cible confortable et bien rodée : croisé dans les pieds du joueur de filet. Enlève-la en cachant où sera ton partenaire : la formation en I ou une fausse interception l'oblige à décider tard et à abandonner un schéma qui marchait.
takeawayFr: Quand un relanceur a rodé sa cible, cache ton joueur de filet — formation en I ou feinte, et sa décision repart de zéro.

focusTag: serving to set up your weapon
scenario: Ad court, 30-30, and you're a righty whose forehand is the weapon. You've served wide six times this game and five returns have come back deep to your backhand corner.
options: Serve T to force the return middle
Serve at the body to cramp their swing
Serve wide again with even more pace
explanation: A T serve takes the returner's angle away, so the reply comes back centrally — the one ball you can run around and load the forehand on. Serving wide again keeps working the door that has sent five straight returns to your backhand.
takeaway: Serve where the return feeds your best shot.

scenario: Break point down at 30-40 in the ad court. Your second serve has been landing short all day, and the righty returner has run around every ball he can reach to hit a forehand.
options: Heavy kick at the body to jam them
Kick out wide to their backhand corner
Flat second serve down the T line
explanation: A body serve leaves a run-around returner no room to open up, and the kick gives net clearance when your arm is tight. Kicking wide to the backhand is textbook, but here it hands him the step-around forehand he has hunted all match.
takeaway: Tight arm, big point: kick into the body.

scenario: Your opponent stands two meters behind the baseline to return. What does this position invite?
options: Wide slice — the extra depth makes the angle drag them off court
Harder flat serves at the same spot
Only T serves
explanation: Deep returners cover pace but not width. A wide slice pulls them farther with every step and opens the whole court for your +1.
takeaway: Deep return position = attack with angle, not speed.
mistakeType: answering depth with pace instead of angle
scenarioTr: Rakibin karşılama için baseline'ın iki metre gerisinde duruyor. Bu pozisyon neyi davet eder?
optionsTr: Geniş kesik servis — mesafe arttıkça açı onu korttan dışarı sürükler
Aynı noktaya daha sert düz servis
explanationTr: Geriden karşılayan hızı karşılar ama genişliği karşılayamaz. Geniş kesik her adımda onu daha da açar ve +1 için kortu boşaltır.
takeawayTr: Geride duran rakibe hızla değil açıyla saldır.
scenarioFr: Ton adversaire se place deux mètres derrière la ligne de fond pour retourner. Qu'est-ce que cette position invite ?
optionsFr: Un slice extérieur — la profondeur supplémentaire l'emmène hors du court
Des services à plat plus forts au même endroit
Uniquement des services au T
explanationFr: Un relanceur reculé couvre la vitesse, pas la largeur. Un slice extérieur l'éloigne à chaque pas et t'ouvre tout le court pour le +1.
takeawayFr: Position de retour reculée = attaque par l'angle, pas par la vitesse.

scenario: You're a lefty serving at 30-40 in the ad court. The righty returner stands well inside the sideline, and he has already hurt you twice today off your T serve.
options: Slice wide, dragging the backhand off court
Heavy kick at the body, then take the middle
Flat down the T again for the ace
explanation: Standing inside the sideline gives your lefty slice its whole runway, and the ball curves further from the backhand the wider it lands. Going back down the T is the tempting variation, but that is the serve he has punished twice.
takeaway: Lefty, ad court, big point: slice it wide.
mistakeType: wasting the lefty advantage on big points

scenario: Set point for you at 5–4, 40–30. What matters most on this first serve?
options: Getting it IN — a made first serve wins most of these points
Maximum pace for a clean ace
Trying your rarest serve for surprise
explanation: First-serve points win at a far higher rate than second-serve points at every level. On set point, a 75% serve in beats a 100% serve out.
takeaway: Big point = make the first serve, even at three-quarter pace.
mistakeType: donating big points with hero serves
scenarioTr: 5–4, 40–30 — set sayın. Bu ilk serviste en önemli şey ne?
optionsTr: İçeri GİRMESİ — atılan ilk servis bu sayıların çoğunu kazandırır
Sürpriz olsun diye en az attığın servisi denemek
explanationTr: Her seviyede ilk servis sayıları, ikinci servis sayılarından çok daha yüksek oranda kazanılır. Set sayısında %75'lik içerideki servis, %100'lük dışarıdakinden iyidir.
takeawayTr: Büyük sayıda ilk servisi içeri at — dörtte üç hızla bile.
scenarioFr: Balle de set pour toi à 5-4, 40-30. Qu'est-ce qui compte le plus sur cette première balle ?
optionsFr: La mettre DEDANS — une première balle en jeu gagne la plupart de ces points
Un maximum de vitesse pour un ace propre
Tenter ton service le plus rare pour surprendre
explanationFr: Les points sur première balle se gagnent à un taux bien supérieur aux points sur deuxième, à tous les niveaux. Sur balle de set, une balle à 75 % dedans vaut mieux qu'une à 100 % dehors.
takeawayFr: Point important = mets la première balle, même aux trois quarts de ta vitesse.

scenario: Your opponent's one-handed backhand looks shaky on high balls. Which second serve exploits this?
options: Kick serve to the backhand shoulder
Slice serve kept low
Flat serve at the forehand
explanation: A kick serve climbs above comfortable contact height — one-handers struggle most above the shoulder on the backhand side.
takeaway: High kick to a one-hander's backhand is a free pressure tool.
mistakeType: serving low to a player who loves low balls
scenarioTr: Rakibin tek el backhand'i yüksek toplarda titrek görünüyor. Hangi ikinci servis bunu kullanır?
explanationTr: Kick servis rahat vuruş yüksekliğinin üstüne tırmanır — tek el backhand omuz üstünde en çok zorlanır.
takeawayTr: Tek el backhand'e yüksek kick bedava baskı aracıdır.
scenarioFr: Le revers à une main de ton adversaire semble fébrile sur les balles hautes. Quelle deuxième balle exploite ça ?
optionsFr: Un service kické sur l'épaule du revers
Un service slicé maintenu bas
Un service à plat sur le coup droit
explanationFr: Un service kické monte au-dessus de la hauteur de frappe confortable — et les revers à une main souffrent surtout au-dessus de l'épaule.
takeawayFr: Un kické haut sur un revers à une main est un outil de pression gratuit.

scenario: You just hit two aces out wide. Next point, your gut says go wide again. What's the smarter frame?
