options: Stay unpredictable — mix, but don't abandon what works until they adjust
Never repeat a serve twice
Always repeat until it misses
explanation: Serving is a probability game: repeat winners until the returner shows an adjustment, then punish the adjustment. React to them, not to superstition.
takeaway: Change your pattern off their adjustment, not your anxiety.
scenarioTr: Az önce açıktan iki as attın. Sonraki sayıda için 'yine açık' diyor. Daha akıllı çerçeve ne?
optionsTr: Okunmaz kal — karıştır ama rakip uyum sağlayana dek işleyeni bırakma
Aynı servisi asla üst üste atma
explanationTr: Servis bir olasılık oyunudur: rakip ayar yapana kadar kazandıranı tekrarla, ayarı görünce onu cezalandır. Batıla değil rakibe tepki ver.
takeawayTr: Deseni kaygına göre değil, rakibin ayarına göre değiştir.
scenarioFr: Tu viens de faire deux aces à l'extérieur. Au point suivant, ton instinct dit d'y retourner. Quel est le bon cadre de pensée ?
optionsFr: Rester imprévisible — varie, mais n'abandonne pas ce qui marche tant qu'il ne s'adapte pas
Ne jamais répéter un service deux fois
Toujours répéter jusqu'à la faute
explanationFr: Servir est un jeu de probabilités : répète ce qui gagne jusqu'à ce que le relanceur montre un ajustement, puis punis cet ajustement. Réagis à lui, pas à une superstition.
takeawayFr: Change de schéma en réaction à son ajustement, pas à ton anxiété.

scenario: 30-30, with two double faults already this game. Watching yourself, you're starting the motion within a second of stepping to the line, before your breathing has settled at all.
options: Bounce, breathe, serve to a spin target
Serve straight away before the doubt builds
Use the full time allowed each point
explanation: A short deliberate reset lets the breathing catch up and gives the swing a spin target to commit to, which is what a rushed motion lacks. Serving straight away to outrun the doubt keeps the shortened motion that produced both faults.
takeaway: Reset the ritual, then commit to a spin target.

scenario: Deuce court against a righty with a huge forehand return. Which first-serve direction limits the damage?
options: T serve — it finds the backhand and cuts the angle
Wide — to his forehand strength
Body — always body
explanation: In the deuce court a T serve arrives at a righty's backhand and gives the returner almost no angle to work with.
takeaway: Deuce T = backhand + no angles for a right-hander.
scenarioTr: Deuce tarafında, forehand karşılaması müthiş bir sağlağa karşısın. Hangi ilk servis yönü hasarı sınırlar?
optionsTr: T servisi — backhand'i bulur ve açıyı keser
explanationTr: Deuce tarafında T servisi sağlağın backhand'ine gider ve karşılayana neredeyse hiç açı bırakmaz.
takeawayTr: Deuce T = sağlak için backhand + açısızlık.
scenarioFr: Côté égalité, face à un droitier au retour de coup droit énorme. Quelle direction de première balle limite les dégâts ?
optionsFr: Le service au T — il trouve le revers et coupe l'angle
Extérieur — sur sa force en coup droit
Sur le corps — toujours le corps
explanationFr: Côté égalité, un service au T arrive sur le revers d'un droitier et ne lui laisse presque aucun angle à exploiter.
takeawayFr: T côté égalité = revers et zéro angle pour un droitier.

scenario: Second set with a strong wind at your back on this end. Three of your flat first serves have flown a foot long already and you're serving at 15-30.
options: Add spin and aim shorter in the box
Keep the target, take pace off the serve
Keep it flat and aim right at the line
explanation: A tailwind adds length, so topspin brings the ball down earlier and a shorter target keeps your margin inside the service line. Just taking pace off is the common fix, but a slow flat serve still rides the wind long.
takeaway: Wind behind you: more spin, shorter target.

scenario: Deuce court, 40-30. Your wide serve drags the returner two steps outside the alley, and the block return floats back crosscourt, landing short of your service line.
options: Forehand into the open ad court, deep
Forehand behind them to the deuce corner
Forehand deep up the middle, then move in
explanation: They are still outside the alley and the short floater gives you time, so the open ad court is the biggest target available. Hitting behind them wrong-foots, but that only pays once they start sprinting early to recover.
takeaway: Wide serve, short reply — hit the space, not the body.
mistakeType: overcomplicating the +1 with the court open

scenario: Your ball toss keeps drifting behind you and serves are sailing long. What's the practical in-match fix?
options: Catch bad tosses and re-toss without penalty
Swing anyway — re-tossing looks weak
Aim lower to compensate
explanation: You're allowed to catch a toss. Swinging at a drifting toss bakes the error in; catching it costs nothing and resets your rhythm.
takeaway: Never swing at a toss you don't trust.
scenarioTr: Top atışın sürekli arkana kaçıyor ve servisler uzun gidiyor. Maç içi pratik çözüm ne?
optionsTr: Kötü atışı tut ve bedelsiz yeniden at
Yine de vur — yeniden atmak zayıf görünür
Telafi için daha alçağa nişan al
explanationTr: Atışı tutmak serbesttir. Kaçan atışa vurmak hatayı içine gömer; tutmak hiçbir şeye mal olmaz ve ritmi sıfırlar.
takeawayTr: Güvenmediğin atışa asla vurma.
scenarioFr: Ton lancer de balle dérive derrière toi et tes services partent longs. Quelle solution concrète en match ?
optionsFr: Rattraper les mauvais lancers et relancer, sans pénalité
Frapper quand même — relancer fait faible
Viser plus bas pour compenser
explanationFr: Tu as le droit de rattraper ton lancer. Frapper un lancer qui dérive intègre la faute ; le rattraper ne coûte rien et remet ton rythme en place.
takeawayFr: Ne frappe jamais un lancer en lequel tu n'as pas confiance.

scenario: Your opponent has chipped fourteen of sixteen returns, all landing short of your service line and below net height. You're serving at 30-30 on a medium-paced hard court.
options: Move in as you land from the serve
Wait for the chip to bounce, then move in
Hold the baseline and rally from there
explanation: Fourteen short chips is a pattern you can move on before the ball lands, and taking it above net height turns their reply into your approach. Waiting for the bounce feels safer, but the ball is dying and you arrive to a low volley.
takeaway: Against a chipper, move in off your own landing.

scenario: Singles, but your opponent has started standing IN on your second serve, taking it at 30–15. What's the message serve?
options: Heavy body kick — jam the incoming returner
Double-down on the same soft second
Wide slice from a defensive toss
explanation: A returner stepping in has shortened their own reaction time. A kicking body serve gives them no room to swing and punishes the aggressive position.
takeaway: When they step in, serve INTO them, not away from them.
mistakeType: serving away from an attacking returner
scenarioTr: Tekler, ama rakip ikinci servisinde İÇERİ girip 30–15'te erken almaya başladı. Mesaj servisi hangisi?
optionsTr: Ağır gövde kick'i — içeri giren rakibi sıkıştır
explanationTr: İçeri giren rakip kendi tepki süresini kısaltmıştır. Gövdeye kick, salınacak yer bırakmaz ve agresif pozisyonu cezalandırır.
takeawayTr: İçeri girene servisten kaçma — üstüne at.
scenarioFr: En simple, ton adversaire s'est mis à AVANCER sur ta deuxième balle et la prend tôt, à 30-15. Quel service fait passer le message ?
optionsFr: Un kick lourd sur le corps — coince le relanceur qui avance
Insister avec la même deuxième balle molle
Un slice extérieur depuis un lancer défensif
explanationFr: Un relanceur qui avance a raccourci son propre temps de réaction. Un service kické sur le corps ne lui laisse pas de place pour armer et punit sa position agressive.
takeawayFr: Quand il avance, sers SUR lui, pas loin de lui.

scenario: Serving from the west end at 3-3, the low sun sits exactly in your toss line. You've missed four of five first serves from this end and made every one from the other.
options: Angle the toss out of the glare
Shift a step along the baseline, same serve
Keep the toss and serve on feel, eyes down
explanation: Angling the toss out of the sun and accepting a spin-first serve keeps your eyes on the ball, the only variable that decides this point. Sliding a step along the baseline rarely helps — a low sun travels with you down the line.
takeaway: Move the toss out of the sun before the score forces you.
mistakeType: refusing to adapt the toss to conditions

scenario: Deuce court, 30-30, a 150 km/h first serve into your forehand that you meet balanced on the baseline. Their backhand has coughed up three short balls already this set.
options: Deep crosscourt to the backhand
Down the line to the backhand corner
Deep up the middle to stay neutral
explanation: Balanced and on time, crosscourt gives you the longest court and the lowest net while feeding the wing already leaking short balls. Down the line reaches the same wing over the highest net with no room, for no extra reward.
takeaway: Balanced return? Longest court, weakest wing.

scenario: Their second serve lands short and sits up every time. What's the positional adjustment?
options: Start a meter inside your usual spot and take it on the rise
Stay in first-serve position to be safe
Back up for more time
explanation: A weak second serve is a free attack — but only if you meet it early. Taking it on the rise steals the server's recovery time.
takeaway: Move your feet UP before the second serve, not your swing speed.
mistakeType: standing deep against weak second serves
scenarioTr: Rakibin ikinci servisi hep kısa düşüp yükseliyor. Pozisyon ayarı ne olmalı?
optionsTr: Normal yerinden bir metre içeride başla ve topu yükselirken al
Güvenli olsun diye ilk servis pozisyonunda kal
explanationTr: Zayıf ikinci servis bedava hücumdur — ama ancak erken karşılarsan. Yükselen topu almak servisçinin toparlanma süresini çalar.
takeawayTr: İkinci servisten önce salınım hızını değil ayaklarını öne taşı.
scenarioFr: Sa deuxième balle tombe court et reste haute à chaque fois. Quel ajustement de position ?
optionsFr: Démarrer un mètre devant ta place habituelle et la prendre à la montée
Rester en position de première balle, par sécurité
Reculer pour avoir plus de temps
explanationFr: Une deuxième balle faible est une attaque offerte — mais seulement si tu la prends tôt. La prendre à la montée vole au serveur son temps de replacement.
takeawayFr: Avance tes appuis avant la deuxième balle, n'accélère pas ton geste.

scenario: Deuce court, 0-30 down on a fast indoor hard court. Their flat first serve has produced four late, framed returns off your backhand in the last two games.
options: Shorten to a block, contact in front
Keep the full swing but start it earlier
Step back a metre and swing normally
explanation: Framed returns mean the racquet is late, and a compact block gets contact in front while borrowing the server's pace. Keeping the full swing and starting earlier sounds like the fix, but a long backswing is what you can't start in time.
takeaway: Late on the return? Cut the swing, not the reaction.

scenario: Break point FOR you. History says their second serve goes to your backhand. What's the plan?
options: Commit early: run around it and hit the forehand return you decided on beforehand
Wait, react, keep every option open
Chip it back safely — it's a big point
explanation: On predictable big-point serves, the returner who has pre-committed wins the exchange. A planned forehand return converts far more break points than neutral reactions.
takeaway: On break points, return with a decision, not a reaction.
scenarioTr: Break sayısı SENDE. İstatistik, ikinci servislerinin backhand'ine geldiğini söylüyor. Plan ne?
optionsTr: Erken karar: dolan ve önceden kararlaştırdığın forehand karşılamayı vur
Bekle, tepki ver, tüm seçenekleri açık tut
explanationTr: Tahmin edilebilir büyük-sayı servislerinde önceden karar vermiş karşılayıcı kazanır. Planlı forehand karşılama, nötr tepkilerden çok daha fazla break çevirir.
takeawayTr: Break sayısında tepkiyle değil kararla karşıla.
scenarioFr: Balle de break POUR toi. L'historique dit que sa deuxième balle part sur ton revers. Quel est le plan ?
optionsFr: T'engager tôt : te décaler et jouer le retour de coup droit décidé à l'avance
Attendre, réagir, garder toutes les options ouvertes
La chipper prudemment — c'est un gros point
explanationFr: Sur les gros points où le service est prévisible, c'est le relanceur qui s'est engagé à l'avance qui gagne l'échange. Un retour de coup droit planifié convertit bien plus de balles de break qu'une réaction neutre.
takeawayFr: Sur balle de break, retourne avec une décision, pas avec une réaction.

scenario: Their kick serve keeps climbing above your backhand shoulder. What's the simplest counter?
options: Step in and take it earlier, before it climbs
Back up and hit it at head height
Swing harder at the high ball
explanation: The kick's weapon is its bounce. Meeting the ball before the apex turns a shoulder-high problem into a waist-high rally ball.
takeaway: Beat the kick with your feet (earlier), not your shoulder (higher).
scenarioTr: Kick servis sürekli backhand omzunun üstüne tırmanıyor. En basit panzehir?
explanationTr: Kick'in silahı sekmesidir. Topu tepe noktasından önce karşılamak, omuz hizası problemini bel hizası ralli topuna çevirir.
takeawayTr: Kick'i omzunla (daha yüksek) değil ayaklarınla (daha erken) yen.
scenarioFr: Son service kické monte sans arrêt au-dessus de ton épaule côté revers. Quelle est la parade la plus simple ?
optionsFr: Avancer et la prendre plus tôt, avant qu'elle monte
Reculer et la frapper à hauteur de tête
Frapper plus fort dans la balle haute
explanationFr: L'arme du kick, c'est son rebond. Prendre la balle avant son sommet transforme un problème à hauteur d'épaule en une balle d'échange à hauteur de hanche.
takeawayFr: Bats le kick avec tes pieds (plus tôt), pas avec ton épaule (plus haut).

scenario: Surprise — they're serving and volleying on big points. What return hurts that most?
options: Low ball at their feet as they close in
High deep lob every time
Hardest possible drive at the open court
explanation: A volleyer's nightmare is contact below net height mid-run. Low at the feet forces a defensive half-volley you can attack.
takeaway: Against the rusher: make their first volley come from their shoelaces.
scenarioTr: Sürpriz — büyük sayılarda servis-vole oynuyorlar. Buna en çok hangi karşılama acı verir?
explanationTr: Volecinin kâbusu koşu ortasında file altından temas etmektir. Ayak dibine alçak top, saldırabileceğin savunmacı bir yarım vole zorlar.
takeawayTr: File koşucusuna karşı ilk voleyi ayakkabı bağından açtır.
scenarioFr: Surprise : il sert-volée sur les gros points. Quel retour lui fait le plus mal ?
optionsFr: Une balle basse dans ses pieds pendant qu'il monte
Un lob haut et profond à chaque fois
La frappe la plus forte possible dans le court ouvert
explanationFr: Le cauchemar d'un volleyeur, c'est une frappe sous le niveau du filet en pleine course. Bas dans les pieds l'oblige à une demi-volée défensive que tu peux attaquer.
takeawayFr: Contre celui qui monte : oblige-le à jouer sa première volée dans ses lacets.

scenario: You're 0–3 down on their serve games without a sniff. What's the strategic reframe for return games?
options: Target one game per set: raise intensity on their second serves and 30–30 points
Accept their serve is too good
Gamble on every single return
explanation: You don't need to win every return game — one break usually decides club sets. Concentrating energy on second serves and score pressure points is efficient aggression.
takeaway: Return games are about ONE well-timed surge, not constant heroics.
mistakeType: even effort distribution across return games
scenarioTr: Rakibin servis oyunlarında 0–3 geridesin, koku bile alamadın. Karşılama oyunları için stratejik çerçeve ne?
optionsTr: Set başına bir oyun hedefle: ikinci servislerde ve 30–30'larda yoğunluğu artır
explanationTr: Her karşılama oyununu kazanman gerekmiyor — kulüp setlerini genelde tek break belirler. Enerjiyi ikinci servislere ve skor baskısı anlarına yığmak verimli agresyondur.
takeawayTr: Karşılama oyunları sürekli kahramanlık değil, İYİ zamanlanmış tek dalgadır.
scenarioFr: Tu es mené 0-3 sans avoir vu la couleur de ses jeux de service. Quel recadrage stratégique pour tes jeux de retour ?
optionsFr: Viser un jeu par set : monter l'intensité sur ses deuxièmes balles et à 30-30
Accepter que son service est trop fort
Tout miser sur chaque retour
explanationFr: Tu n'as pas besoin de gagner tous les jeux de retour — un seul break décide généralement d'un set en club. Concentrer ton énergie sur les deuxièmes balles et les points sous pression, c'est de l'agressivité efficace.
takeawayFr: Les jeux de retour se gagnent par UNE poussée bien placée, pas par de l'héroïsme permanent.

scenario: You keep getting caught flat-footed on returns. What's missing?
options: A split step timed to their contact
A bigger backswing
Standing perfectly still for stability
explanation: The split step at the server's contact loads both legs so your first move is explosive in either direction. Without it, you're reacting a beat late.
takeaway: No split step, no return. Time it to their hit.
mistakeType: missing the split step on return
scenarioTr: Karşılamalarda sürekli hazırlıksız yakalanıyorsun. Eksik ne?
optionsTr: Rakibin vuruş anına zamanlanmış split step
explanationTr: Servisçinin temas anındaki split step iki bacağı da yükler; ilk hareketin iki yöne de patlayıcı olur. Onsuz bir tempo geç kalırsın.
takeawayTr: Split step yoksa karşılama yok. Vuruş anına zamanla.
scenarioFr: Tu te fais surprendre les pieds plantés sur les retours. Qu'est-ce qui manque ?
optionsFr: Un split-step calé sur sa frappe
Une préparation plus ample
Rester parfaitement immobile pour la stabilité
explanationFr: Le split-step au moment de la frappe du serveur charge les deux jambes pour que ton premier appui soit explosif des deux côtés. Sans lui, tu réagis avec un temps de retard.
takeawayFr: Pas de split-step, pas de retour. Cale-le sur sa frappe.

scenario: Third set on their serve. Across five service games their toss has drifted a foot to their right before every slice, and stayed over the head for the kick. How do you use it?
options: Lean that way as their racquet drops
Commit to the side as the toss leaves the hand
Wait for the bounce, then chase it down
explanation: Leaning at the racquet drop uses the read but still leaves you time to stop if this one is different, which is the point of a half-step. Committing at the toss is the greedy version — a server who sees the lean serves the other way.
takeaway: Use the tell late: lean at the racquet drop, not the toss.

scenario: You hit a deep return, watch it land, and their reply passes you down the line. Replaying it, you were still standing where you returned from when they made contact.
options: Move as you finish the follow-through
Move once the return lands on their side
Move when you read their swing direction
explanation: Recovery starts on your own follow-through because it is the only free time in the exchange, and by their contact you must already be split and centred. Waiting for the ball to land leaves you two steps short of any ball hit on the rise.
takeaway: Start recovering on your follow-through, not on their bounce.

scenario: You love the down-the-line return winner. When is it actually the right call?
options: On a short, slow serve when you're balanced inside the court
On every big point
Whenever you feel hot
explanation: Down the line crosses the highest net and gives the shortest court. It needs a short ball, early contact and balance — otherwise it's a donation dressed as bravery.
takeaway: Line returns are earned by the serve's weakness, not your mood.
scenarioTr: Paralel karşılama sayısını seviyorsun. Gerçekten ne zaman doğru karar?
optionsTr: Kısa ve yavaş serviste, kortun içinde dengedeyken
explanationTr: Paralel, filenin en yüksek yerinden geçer ve en kısa kortu sunar. Kısa top, erken temas ve denge ister — yoksa cesaret kılığında hediyedir.
takeawayTr: Paralel karşılamayı ruh hâlin değil servisin zayıflığı hak ettirir.

scenario: The serve jams into your body. What's the escape move?
options: Quick side-shuffle to create space and take it with the backhand block
Lean back and flick with wrists
Take a full swing from your chest
explanation: Against body serves, space is everything. A fast lateral shuffle plus compact backhand block is the highest-percentage escape at every level.
takeaway: Move yourself, not just the racquet, on body serves.
scenarioTr: Servis gövdene saplandı. Kaçış hamlesi ne?
optionsTr: Hızlı yana kayıp yer aç ve backhand blokla al
explanationTr: Gövde servisine karşı her şey alan yaratmaktır. Hızlı yana kayış + kompakt backhand blok her seviyede en yüksek yüzdeli kaçıştır.
takeawayTr: Gövde servisinde sadece raketi değil kendini oynat.

scenario: Ad court, their righty slice pulls you wide. Balanced but stretched — where's the smart return?
options: High and deep crosscourt to reset with time
Flat down the line on the stretch
Sharp short angle back
explanation: Stretched wide, your priorities are height for safety and depth for time. Deep crosscourt travels the longest distance while you recover.
takeaway: Stretched = high, deep, crosscourt. Save the line for balance.
mistakeType: changing direction off a deep defensive ball
scenarioTr: Ad tarafı, sağlağın kesiği seni açığa sürükledi. Dengedesin ama gerginsin — akıllı karşılama nereye?
optionsTr: Yüksek ve derin çapraza — zamanla sıfırla
explanationTr: Açılmışken önceliğin güvenlik için yükseklik, zaman için derinliktir. Derin çapraz, sen toparlanırken en uzun yolu kat eder.
takeawayTr: Gerildiysen = yüksek, derin, çapraz. Paraleli dengeye sakla.

scenario: Two sets in against the same server. You've stood in the same spot on every return, and they've hit the same wide slice on eleven of their last twelve first serves.
options: Move your starting depth around between points
Stand a metre further back for the rest of the set
Keep your spot and read the toss instead
explanation: Eleven of twelve to one target means they are aiming off a fixed reference, so changing your depth point to point forces a fresh aim every time. Moving back once only gives them a new fixed target to groove against within a game.
takeaway: Keep moving the target they're aiming at.

scenario: You've missed three first-serve returns in a row against a 190 km/h serve and you're 0-40 down. Their two second serves this set both landed at around 140 km/h.
options: Land first returns, attack the seconds
Attack each serve until one finally lands
Chip returns back and start the rally
explanation: Against a 190 km/h serve a return that simply lands deep is already a win, and the 140 km/h second serves are where break points are actually built. Attacking each serve until one lands feels brave, but it donates points you cannot afford at 0-40.
takeaway: Survive the first serve, hunt the second.

scenario: Deep crosscourt rally, ball after ball. When do you earn the right to go down the line?
options: When you get a shorter or slower ball you can meet inside the baseline
Whenever you're bored of crosscourt
On the deepest ball they hit
explanation: Changing direction off a deep ball means hitting over the high net into the short court while off balance. The short/slow ball is the green light.
takeaway: Change direction on YOUR terms — off the short ball.
scenarioTr: Derin çapraz ralli, top üstüne top. Paralele dönme hakkını ne zaman kazanırsın?
optionsTr: Baseline içinde karşılayabileceğin daha kısa/yavaş top geldiğinde
explanationTr: Derin toptan yön değiştirmek, dengesizken yüksek fileden kısa korta vurmak demektir. Kısa/yavaş top yeşil ışıktır.
takeawayTr: Yönü KENDİ şartlarında değiştir — kısa topta.

scenario: 30–30 on your serve in a neutral crosscourt rally. Your opponent stands right on the baseline, takes everything early, and every flat ball you hit comes back faster than you sent it.
options: Add height and land it deeper
Flatten out and hit through them harder
Go for a short angle to drag them in
explanation: A deep, heavy ball pushes an early-taking opponent behind the baseline and steals the timing their whole game runs on. Hitting through them harder is the tempting reply, but pace into their strike zone is what they redirect.
takeaway: Beat an early taker with depth, not speed.

scenario: You've pulled them wide and they're sprinting to cover the open court. Where's the winner now?
options: Behind them — back where they came from
The open court they're sprinting toward
Straight at them
explanation: Once a fast opponent commits to covering the open court, their momentum can't reverse. Hitting behind them wrong-foots the recovery.
takeaway: Against fast runners: open the court, then hit behind.
mistakeType: always hitting to the open court
scenarioTr: Rakibi açığa çektin, açık kortu kapatmak için depar atıyor. Sayı şimdi nerede?
explanationTr: Hızlı rakip açık kortu kapatmaya karar verince momentumu geri dönemez. Arkasına vurmak toparlanmayı ters ayakta yakalar.
takeawayTr: Hızlı koşucuya: kortu aç, sonra arkasına vur.

scenario: You're dragged deep behind the baseline, barely reaching the ball. What buys you back into the point?
options: A high, deep ball down the middle — time to recover
A flat counter-winner attempt
A desperate drop shot
explanation: Height equals time. A high deep middle ball travels slowly, lands far from both winners' corners, and lets you rebuild your court position.
takeaway: In trouble, buy time with height — not risk with pace.
scenarioTr: Baseline'ın çok gerisine sürüklendin, topa zor yetişiyorsun. Seni sayıya ne geri sokar?
optionsTr: Ortadan yüksek ve derin top — toparlanma zamanı
explanationTr: Yükseklik = zaman. Ortadan yüksek derin top yavaş gider, iki sayı köşesinden de uzağa düşer ve pozisyonunu yeniden kurmana izin verir.
takeawayTr: Zordayken hızla risk değil, yükseklikle zaman satın al.

scenario: Mid-rally, their ball lands near the service line and sits up. What's the mindset?
options: Attack ball — move in, hit deep to a corner, follow it forward
Just another rally ball back crosscourt
Wait for an even shorter one
explanation: Short + high = the rally's reward. Hitting deep off it while moving forward converts your earned advantage into court position and pressure.
takeaway: Recognize the short ball early; the winner is two shots later.
mistakeType: resetting instead of attacking short balls
scenarioTr: Ralli ortasında rakibin topu servis çizgisi civarına düşüp yükseliyor. Zihniyet ne olmalı?
optionsTr: Hücum topu — içeri gir, köşeye derin vur, arkasından öne devam et
explanationTr: Kısa + yüksek = rallinin ödülü. Öne hareket ederken derin vurmak, kazandığın avantajı pozisyona ve baskıya çevirir.
takeawayTr: Kısa topu erken tanı; sayı iki vuruş sonradadır.

scenario: You want more inside-out forehands (your weapon). Which rally ball creates them?
options: A deep ball to their backhand — the weak crosscourt reply lands in your run-around zone
Any ball down the middle
Short angles to their forehand
explanation: Pressure their backhand deep and the typical reply is a slower crosscourt into your backhand corner — exactly where you can run around and dictate inside-out.
takeaway: Your forehand hunt starts two shots earlier, on their backhand.
mistakeType: waiting for weapons instead of building them
scenarioTr: Silahın olan inside-out forehand'i daha çok istiyorsun. Hangi ralli topu onu yaratır?
optionsTr: Backhand'ine derin top — zayıf çapraz cevap dolanma bölgene düşer
explanationTr: Backhand'ine derin baskı yap; tipik cevap, backhand köşene gelen yavaş çaprazdır — tam dolanıp inside-out ile yöneteceğin yer.
takeawayTr: Forehand avın iki vuruş önce, rakibin backhand'inde başlar.

scenario: 4–5, 30–40 and a set point against you. You're in a neutral forehand exchange from the deuce corner, both of you behind the baseline, and nothing on their side is open yet.
options: Go crosscourt again, over the low middle
Change direction down the line
Drive it flat up the middle at them
explanation: With nothing open, crosscourt buys the lowest net, the longest court and the shortest recovery, three margins for free on a set point. Changing direction down the line off a deep ball asks for the highest net and the shortest court.
takeaway: On big points, choose the direction with the most margin.

scenario: You keep losing 6+ shot rallies by going for too much on ball five. What's the training cue?
options: Raise your 'boring threshold': no winner attempts until a genuinely short ball
Go for winners earlier, on ball three
Avoid long rallies entirely
explanation: Club rallies are lost, not won — the player who can stand one more neutral ball usually collects the error. Patience is a trained skill.
takeaway: Win the boredom contest; the short ball always comes.
scenarioTr: 6+ vuruşluk rallileri beşinci topta fazlasını isteyerek kaybediyorsun. Antrenman komutu ne?
optionsTr: 'Sıkıcılık eşiğini' yükselt: gerçekten kısa top gelmeden sayı denemesi yok
Sayıyı daha erken, üçüncü topta dene
explanationTr: Kulüp rallileri kazanılmaz, kaybedilir — bir nötr topa daha dayanabilen genelde hatayı toplar. Sabır çalışılan bir beceridir.
takeawayTr: Sıkılma yarışını kazan; kısa top eninde sonunda gelir.

scenario: Your opponent loves pace and rhythm — everything you hit hard comes back harder. What breaks their engine?
options: High, heavy loops that make them generate their own power
More pace to out-hit them
Standing closer to the baseline
explanation: Pace-lovers feed on your energy. A slow high loop above shoulder height forces them to create power from nothing — where their timing and patience crack.
takeaway: Starve the counter-puncher: no pace to borrow.
scenarioTr: Rakip hız ve ritim âşığı — sert vurduğun her şey daha sert dönüyor. Motorunu ne bozar?
optionsTr: Kendi gücünü üretmeye zorlayan yüksek, ağır loop'lar
explanationTr: Hız sevenler senin enerjinle beslenir. Omuz üstü yavaş yüksek loop, gücü sıfırdan üretmeye zorlar — zamanlaması ve sabrı orada çatlar.
takeawayTr: Kontracıyı aç bırak: ödünç alacak hız verme.

scenario: You crack a short sharp crosscourt angle from the deuce side and they only just reach it, stretched wide outside the alley. You're still standing a metre inside the baseline after the shot.
options: Follow it in and close the net
Recover to the centre mark as usual
Hold deep behind the baseline and reset
explanation: Pulling them that wide also handed them a counter-angle, and from a metre inside the baseline the only way to cover it is forward. Recovering to the centre mark leaves the short angle you just opened completely free.
takeaway: Insure every angle you hit by closing behind it.
mistakeType: admiring an angle instead of closing

scenario: Serving at 4–5, 30–30. Their heavy topspin keeps kicking above your backhand shoulder, and your last three replies floated short from a metre behind the baseline.
options: Back up a step and take it later
Stand in and take it early on the rise
Drive it flat at shoulder height
explanation: One step back lets the kick drop into your strike zone, where the same backhand goes deep instead of floating short. Taking it on the rise is the brave answer, but a rising kick above the shoulder is the hardest contact you own.
takeaway: Give a kicking ball one step and it becomes a normal ball.
mistakeType: recovering to the hash instead of the bisector

scenario: 2–2 in the first, backhand to backhand crosscourt, both steady. Your backhand is the weaker wing and you've missed two of the last five, while they take it early from on the baseline.
options: Loop it higher and heavier crosscourt
Rip it down the line to their forehand
Flatten out and take it earlier
explanation: You are losing this exchange, so change what the ball looks like before you change where it goes; height and weight cost nothing and push an early taker back. Ripping down the line is the classic escape and the classic error.
takeaway: Change ball quality before ball direction.
mistakeType: line gamble to escape a losing exchange

scenario: You change ends at 3–2 and now you're hitting into a stiff wind. Your last two flat drives died a metre inside the baseline, and she's floating replies from well behind hers.
options: Swing full and aim near the lines
Add spin and aim well inside the lines
Take pace off and keep it safe
explanation: A headwind brakes and holds every ball, so full swings land short of the lines you would normally fear; this is the set to attack. Adding spin and margin is the with-the-wind answer, and into the wind it just feeds her short balls.
takeaway: Into the wind, swing free; with it, add spin.

scenario: They push every ball back high and deep, refusing errors. Rallying from the baseline is a swamp. What's the structural answer?
options: Take the high ball early out of the air or on the rise and come IN — finish at the net
Out-moonball them for hours
Aim for outright winners from the baseline
explanation: Pushers beat you in their arena — long floaty rallies. Taking time away (swing volley, on-the-rise) and finishing at net moves the contest to an arena they hate.
takeaway: Don't out-wait a waiter. Change the arena: come in.
mistakeType: baseline war of attrition vs a pusher
scenarioTr: Her topu yüksek ve derin itiyor, hata yapmayı reddediyor. Baseline rallisi bataklık. Yapısal cevap ne?
optionsTr: Yüksek topu havada ya da yükselirken erken al ve İÇERİ gir — fileye bitir
explanationTr: İtici (pusher) seni kendi arenasında yener — uzun, süzülen ralliler. Zamanını çalmak (kuvvetli vole, yükselirken vuruş) ve filede bitirmek, maçı nefret ettiği arenaya taşır.
takeawayTr: Bekleyeni bekleyerek yenemezsin. Arenayı değiştir: içeri gir.

scenario: 30–30 and they float a short ball that lands near your service line and sits up. All match you've stopped, planted and floated these back from mid-court while they strolled back into position.
options: Move through it and follow it in
Plant, hit it hard, and stay back
Let it drop lower, then drive it
explanation: A mid-court ball is a transition ball: momentum through contact adds free pace and leaves you at the net for the reply. Planting and staying back is exactly what has been floating them back all match.
takeaway: Let your feet finish the short ball, not your arm.

scenario: 3–3, 30–15. Their slice lands short in your deuce court and you step inside the baseline while they recover to the centre. Their backhand has been a floating chip all match.
options: Approach down the line to the backhand
Approach crosscourt to the open court
Approach deep down the middle
explanation: The line approach travels the shorter distance and points you straight at the chip backhand, so you can shade the line and cover the pass. Crosscourt into the open court feels bigger but leaves the line pass behind you.
takeaway: Approach down the line, then shade the line.
mistakeType: crosscourt approaches that open the pass

scenario: First volley after coming in — where does it go if no easy kill is on?
options: Deep to the baseline, usually behind or at their backhand
Short angle drop volley
As hard as possible anywhere
explanation: A deep first volley keeps them pinned and buys you a step closer for the real finishing volley. Drop volleys from the service line are donations.
takeaway: First volley = deep and boring. Second volley = the kill.
mistakeType: attempting an angled volley from too far back
scenarioTr: İçeri girdikten sonraki ilk vole — kolay bitirme yoksa nereye?
optionsTr: Baseline'a derin, genelde backhand'e ya da arkasına
explanationTr: Derin ilk vole rakibi geride çiviler ve asıl bitirici vole için bir adım daha yaklaşmanı sağlar. Servis çizgisinden drop vole hediyedir.
takeawayTr: İlk vole = derin ve sıkıcı. İkinci vole = bitirici.

scenario: You keep getting passed even when your approach is good. Video shows you running through the approach. What's missing?
options: A split step the moment THEY start their swing
More speed to the net
Standing still at the service line
explanation: If you're mid-sprint at their contact, you can't change direction. The split at their swing start converts your momentum into readiness both ways.
takeaway: Sprint between their shots; split AT their shot.
scenarioTr: Yaklaşman iyiyken bile pas yiyorsun. Videoda yaklaşmayı koşarak geçtiğin görülüyor. Eksik ne?
optionsTr: RAKİP salınıma başladığı anda split step
explanationTr: Onun temasında depar hâlindeysen yön değiştiremezsin. Salınım başında split, momentumunu iki yöne de hazırlığa çevirir.
takeawayTr: Vuruşları arasında koş; vuruşunun ANINDA split yap.

scenario: Easy volley, opponent scrambling from your left to your right. Open court right, or behind them left?
options: Behind them if they're sprinting hard — momentum can't stop
Always open court, no exceptions
Down the middle
explanation: The open court is right ONLY if they haven't committed. Against a full sprint, the ball behind them is untouchable because reversing costs two steps.
takeaway: Volley to where they CAN'T go, which isn't always where they AREN'T.
mistakeType: always hitting to the open court
scenarioTr: Kolay vole, rakip solundan sağına koşturuyor. Sağdaki açık kort mu, soluna arkasına mı?
explanationTr: Açık kort ancak rakip karar vermemişse doğrudur. Tam depara karşı arkasına atılan top dokunulmazdır; geri dönmek iki adıma mal olur.
takeawayTr: Voleyi olmadığı yere değil, GİDEMEYECEĞİ yere at.

scenario: A deep lob goes up over you. What's the footwork that saves the smash?
options: Turn sideways and cross-step back, racquet up early
Backpedal facing the net
Let every deep lob bounce
explanation: Backpedaling is slow and ends in falling smashes. Turning sideways converts the retreat into athletic strides while the early racquet prep keeps the smash compact.
takeaway: Turn, cross-step, racquet up — never backpedal to a lob.
scenarioTr: Üstünden derin lob yükseliyor. Smacı kurtaran ayak işi ne?
optionsTr: Yan dön, çapraz adımla geri git, raketi erken kaldır
explanationTr: Geri geri koşmak yavaştır ve düşerek smaçla biter. Yan dönüş geri çekilmeyi atletik adımlara çevirir; erken raket hazırlığı smacı kompakt tutar.
takeawayTr: Dön, çapraz adım, raket yukarı — loba asla geri geri koşma.

focusTag: when to let the lob bounce
scenario: Very high, very deep lob on a windy day. Take it in the air or let it bounce?
options: Let it bounce — the wind punishes airborne timing; smash after the bounce
Always in the air, look strong
Run around it and forehand
explanation: On high wind-blown lobs, the bounce resets the chaos: predictable ball drop, set feet, controlled smash. Air smashes there are coin flips.
takeaway: Wind + towering lob = bounce smash.
scenarioTr: Rüzgârlı günde çok yüksek, çok derin lob. Havada mı alırsın, sektirir misin?
optionsTr: Sektir — rüzgâr havadaki zamanlamayı cezalandırır; sekmeden sonra smaçla
explanationTr: Rüzgârda yüksek loblarda sekme kaosu sıfırlar: öngörülebilir düşüş, oturmuş ayaklar, kontrollü smaç. Orada havadan smaç yazı-turadır.
takeawayTr: Rüzgâr + kule gibi lob = sektirip smaç.

scenario: 40–15, you're two metres from the net with a floater arriving at chest height. They just chased a deep ball and are still back-pedalling well behind the baseline.
options: Drop it short over the low net
Punch it deep into the open corner
Angle it wide past the sideline
explanation: Two metres from the net with contact above the tape, the drop travels barely a metre and their momentum is already going the wrong way. Punching deep is right from the service line, but here it feeds a player parked back there.
takeaway: Drop only when you're close in and they're going backwards.
mistakeType: drop volleys against a ready opponent

scenario: You've approached deep to the backhand corner and closed in behind it. It's 30–30 and they have already lobbed you twice this set from that corner. Where do you stop?
options: Stop 2–3 metres from the net, in the box
Close right in, a metre off the net
Hold at the service line and volley
explanation: Two to three metres in is the only band that still reaches the dipping ball yet lets you turn and run down a lob. Crowding the net is tempting after a good approach, but against someone already lobbing you it invites the same shot.
takeaway: Own the middle of the box, not the net cord.

scenario: You're forced to volley below net height. What's the shot's job?
options: Depth and safety — lift it deep, decline the winner attempt
Sharp angle winner anyway
Drop volley — it's already low
explanation: Below net height you're defending at the net. Lifting deep resets the exchange for a better next volley; forcing winners from there feeds the net tape.
takeaway: Low volley = survive deep now, kill the NEXT one.
scenarioTr: File altından vole yapmaya zorlandın. Vuruşun görevi ne?
optionsTr: Derinlik ve güvenlik — derine kaldır, sayı denemesini reddet
explanationTr: File altında filede savunmadasın. Derine kaldırmak alışverişi bir sonraki daha iyi vole için sıfırlar; oradan sayı zorlamak file bandını besler.
takeawayTr: Alçak vole = şimdi derinle hayatta kal, SONRAKİNİ öldür.

focusTag: which balls not to follow in
scenario: 1–1 in the third, they slide a low skidding slice that dies short and you have to scoop it up from below net height. They're balanced on the baseline and have passed you twice off this exact ball.
options: Lift it deep and stay back
Follow it in and close the net
Chip it short and sprint forward
explanation: A ball lifted from below the net arrives slow and rising, so staying back keeps the rally neutral instead of handing them a target. Following it in is the habit that has already cost you two points against a balanced passer.
takeaway: Approach behind balls that hurt them, not ones that hurried you.

scenario: Caught mid-court, ball at your feet — forced half-volley. Key technical priority?
options: Stay low with a short block, aim deep middle
Big swing to generate pace
Jump back to make room
explanation: The half-volley is a timing shot: knees low, compact face-controlled block, target deep middle. Any extra swing multiplies the error.
takeaway: Half-volley: low body, quiet hands, boring target.
scenarioTr: Orta kortta yakalandın, top ayak dibinde — mecburi yarım vole. Teknik öncelik ne?
optionsTr: Alçakta kal, kısa blok, ortaya derin hedefle
explanationTr: Yarım vole bir zamanlama vuruşudur: dizler alçak, raket yüzü kontrollü kompakt blok, hedef ortadan derin. Fazladan her salınım hatayı katlar.
takeawayTr: Yarım vole: alçak gövde, sakin eller, sıkıcı hedef.

scenario: 30–30, you're inside the service box and their lob comes up short, floating above your backhand shoulder. They've stopped in the middle of the baseline to watch it.
options: Punch it deep down the line
Angle it short with soft hands
Swing hard to end it there
explanation: The high backhand volley has no natural power, so a firm punch deep down the line is the version that stays honest and keeps them pinned. The soft short angle is the fashionable choice and the one that dumps into the net.
takeaway: High backhand volley: punch it deep, don't paint it.
mistakeType: getting cute on high backhand volleys

scenario: Slow floaty ball at shoulder height while you're inside the baseline. Swinging volley or let it bounce?
options: Swinging volley — take the time away while moving forward
Always let it bounce for safety
Regular punch volley from there
explanation: Letting a floater bounce gives a retreating opponent free seconds. The swinging volley, taken while closing, compresses their recovery and finishes points early.
takeaway: Floaters inside the baseline are yours — take them out of the air.
scenarioTr: Baseline içindeyken omuz hizasında yavaş süzülen top. Kuvvetli vole mi, sektirmek mi?
optionsTr: Kuvvetli (swing) vole — öne kapanırken zamanını çal
explanationTr: Süzülen topu sektirmek geri kaçan rakibe bedava saniyeler verir. Kapanırken vurulan kuvvetli vole toparlanmasını sıkıştırır ve sayıyı erken bitirir.
takeawayTr: Baseline içindeki süzülen toplar senindir — havada al.

focusTag: reading the pass at the net
scenario: 30–30, you're two metres from the net and they're set up balanced for the pass. You've lunged early all set and twice they've changed direction at the last instant.
options: Split-step and move after contact
Lean to the open side before they swing
Back up a step to buy reaction time
explanation: Reading the ball off their strings is slower but never wrong, and from two metres in you can still reach both passing lanes. Leaning early is why they've beaten you twice: a late changer only needs to see you move first.
takeaway: Move after their contact, never before it.

scenario: You hit a solid deep first volley from the service line. What's your very next move?
options: Close 2–3 steps toward the net for the finishing volley
Stay exactly where you are
Retreat toward the baseline
explanation: Each good volley earns you ground. Closing after the first volley shrinks their passing angles and turns the second volley into a putaway.
takeaway: Volley, then MOVE — the net rewards the greedy.
scenarioTr: Servis çizgisinden sağlam derin bir ilk vole vurdun. Hemen sonraki hamlen ne?
optionsTr: Bitirici vole için fileye 2–3 adım kapan
explanationTr: Her iyi vole sana alan kazandırır. İlk voleden sonra kapanmak pas açılarını daraltır ve ikinci voleyi bitirişe çevirir.
takeawayTr: Vole at, sonra YÜRÜ — file açgözlüyü ödüllendirir.

scenario: Rain stops play for 25 minutes while you lead 6–4, 3–2. In your last delayed match you came back cold and dropped the first two games after the restart.
options: Keep moving through the break: skips and shadow swings
Sit still and stay calm to save energy for later
Use the break to plan new patterns for their backhand
explanation: A stoppage drops heart rate and reaction speed long before it touches your tactics, so movement keeps the body at match temperature. Sitting still to save energy feels sensible and is exactly how those first two games went last time.
takeaway: Keep moving through the break — come back warm.

scenario: You serve at 4–3, 40–0. Twice already today you have been pulled from 40–0 back to deuce, both times after opening the point with a second-ball drop shot.
options: Play the point exactly as you would at deuce
Go for the ace and end the game right now
Take pace off to guarantee the first serve in
explanation: Games are lost at 40–0 by treating the points as spare, so deuce-point discipline is what actually closes it out. Going for the ace swaps a rehearsed pattern for a low-percentage one at the score that has already cost you twice.
takeaway: Play 40–0 like it is deuce.

scenario: Serving for the set at 5–4, 0–0. Your arm feels heavy, both practice tosses drifted behind your head, and you catch yourself planning the changeover.
options: Run your bounce count and pick one serve target
Open with your biggest serve to settle the game fast
Remind yourself it is only four points to the set
explanation: Pressure inflates the future, and a bounce count plus one target shrinks the game back to a task the body already knows. Opening with your biggest serve puts a tight arm behind a low-margin ball and usually starts the game 0–15.
takeaway: Big moment, small focus.
mistakeType: outcome thinking while serving for it

scenario: At 4–5, 30–30 your last four forehands landed inside the service line. Your footwork and between-point tempo are normal; the swing is decelerating at contact.
options: Swing full at a bigger target, high and deep middle
Slow your tempo right down and take extra time
Shorten the point by approaching behind the next ball
explanation: Short, decelerating strokes at normal tempo are choking, which is over-control, so the cure is a full swing at a larger target. Slowing down further is the fix for panic, and here it adds more control to a stroke already dying of it.
takeaway: Pushing, not rushing? Swing bigger, aim bigger.

scenario: Three straight unforced errors, all forehands into the net from mid-court, and the last two came on balls you had plenty of time for. You serve at 2–3, 15–30.
options: Two shots high over the net and deep to the middle
Slice the next few forehands to get the ball in
Step in and take the next short ball early
explanation: Net errors from mid-court mean the swing has shrunk, so two high, deep balls restore clearance and contact before tactics resume. Slicing to get the ball in keeps that same short swing and hands them the mid-court to attack.
takeaway: Break a streak with height and depth.

scenario: From 4–1 up you are 4–4. The lead came from wide serve plus forehand, but for three games you have been rallying crosscourt from behind the baseline.
options: Go back to the wide serve and first forehand pattern
Add pace and flatten out to steal a quick game
Extend rallies and wait for their level to drop
explanation: Leads slide because the winning pattern quietly stops being played, so restoring the wide serve and forehand is the repair. Adding pace to steal a game raises your error rate at the score where cheap points are most expensive.
takeaway: Lost the lead? Replay what built it.
mistakeType: playing at the opponent's hot tempo

scenario: You lead the tiebreak 4–2 with both of your serves coming up. The mini-break arrived on their double fault rather than on a winner of yours.
options: Serve the two patterns that have held all match
Go bigger on both serves to extend the lead
Take something off and make them play a rally
explanation: A breaker lead is protected by the quality of your own point starts, so serve the patterns that have held all match. Going bigger to extend the lead is how players hand back a mini-break they were gifted rather than earned.
takeaway: Protect a breaker lead by giving nothing away.
mistakeType: gifting cheap points early in tiebreaks

scenario: Third set, 2–5 down, legs empty. Since you started walking with your head down, your opponent has cut their between-point time and is serving faster.
options: Walk upright to the back fence and reset there
Let the frustration out visibly so it does not build
Go quiet, skip the routine and save what is left
explanation: Opponents read posture, and an upright walk keeps their doubt alive while your routine keeps you in the match. Venting visibly to release frustration is the exact signal that has them serving faster and freer.
takeaway: Your posture talks — decide what it says.

scenario: They have hit four clean winners in four points to break you. Across the whole first set they hit six winners in total, most of them off short balls you gave them.
options: Keep your patterns and make them repeat it for a game
Match them and go for your own winners earlier
Push higher and deeper and take the pace right off
explanation: Four winners in four points sits far above their set-long rate, so holding your patterns lets that rate pull them back. Matching them winner for winner turns their short streak into your long one, since your risky shots are the newer habit.
takeaway: Let a hot streak cool — keep your patterns.

scenario: You have lost to this opponent twice, both times by feeding their forehand from the middle. Warm-up ends in two minutes and your head is full of half-plans.
options: One behaviour: deep to the backhand until a short ball
Five patterns, one for each way the match can go
A target score: level or better after four games
explanation: A single behavioural instruction survives adrenaline and answers the exact pattern that beat you twice. Five patterns for five scenarios is the plan that vanishes on the first big point, because choosing between them costs time you do not have.
takeaway: One sentence, one behaviour — that is a plan.

scenario: After a 24-shot rally at 30–30 your chest is heaving and your hands are shaking slightly. You have roughly fifteen seconds before you have to serve.
options: Turn away and take three long, slow exhales
Walk to the fence and let it settle by itself
Serve now while the rhythm of the rally is warm
explanation: A long exhale is the fastest legal brake on heart rate and steadies the hands before the toss. Letting it settle by itself works too, but it needs longer than the fifteen seconds you have, so you serve with a racing chest.
takeaway: Exhale longer than you inhale, then serve.

scenario: Third set at 3–3, legs heavy and cramp threatening, so you cannot chase every ball. Their second serve has landed short of the service line all match and you have won seven of ten points on it.
options: Spend on second-serve returns and your own first points
Attack the net at every chance to shorten the points
Take pace off everywhere and hold on for a tiebreak
explanation: Fatigue forces triage, and that short second serve is where each unit of energy buys the most scoreboard. Attacking the net at every chance spends the same legs on points you were already winning from the baseline.
takeaway: Tired legs go where the breaks are.

scenario: You netted a sitting forehand volley at 30–30 and lost the point. You are serving at 4–4 and you can still hear yourself replaying the miss as you line up.
options: Give yourself one instruction: step in and finish through
Tell yourself you are the better player and move on
Work out why the volley missed before you serve
explanation: A short instructional cue converts the miss into the one correction your next volley needs and fills attention with a task. Working out why it missed turns a service point into a technique lesson, and the next point pays the bill.
takeaway: Give yourself an instruction, not a verdict.

scenario: You are a level above today's opponent and it is 3–3. This set you have tried two drop shots and three down-the-line winners, while your crosscourt rally pattern has barely appeared.
options: Go back to executing your normal crosscourt pattern
Raise the risk further to pull away quickly
Add spin and depth and wait for them to miss
explanation: Against a weaker opponent the scoreline slips because execution gets replaced by experiments, so running your ordinary pattern properly is the fix. Raising the risk to pull away is the same drift with a bigger swing on it.
takeaway: Compete against your standard, not their level.

scenario: You have dropped the first three games in four of your last five matches. Today you reach the club fifteen minutes early and a practice court is free.
options: Jog and rally until you sweat before the match hit
Start the match softly and ease into full swings
Save the legs and use the five-minute hit to warm up
explanation: Most first-game nerves are a cold body, and arriving already sweating removes the tightness that has cost you three games four times over. Easing into full swings only postpones the problem into the games that decide the set.
takeaway: Sweat before the first point, not during game four.

scenario: A ball splits you and your partner down the middle. Who takes it, by default?
options: The player with the forehand in the middle
Whoever is closer to the net post
Whoever called 'yours' first
explanation: The middle forehand takes the center ball by default — stronger shot, better reach across. Agree on it BEFORE the match so nobody freezes.
takeaway: Default rules end hesitation: middle = forehand's ball.
scenarioTr: Top seninle partnerinin tam ortasından geliyor. Varsayılan olarak kim alır?
explanationTr: Orta topu varsayılan olarak ortadaki forehand alır — daha güçlü vuruş, daha iyi uzanma. Maçtan ÖNCE anlaşın ki kimse donmasın.
takeawayTr: Varsayılan kurallar tereddüdü bitirir: orta = forehand'in topu.

scenario: Your partner is serving. What is your actual job at the net?
options: Be a threat: shift with the serve, fake poaches, take anything floating
Stand still and avoid getting hit
Watch the returner's face
explanation: A static net player is furniture. Movement — real and faked — shrinks the returner's targets and turns weak returns into your putaways.
takeaway: At net on serve: move every point, even when you don't touch the ball.
scenarioTr: Partnerin servis atıyor. Filedeki gerçek işin ne?
optionsTr: Tehdit ol: servisle birlikte kay, poach çakması yap, süzüleni kap
explanationTr: Duran file oyuncusu mobilyadır. Hareket — gerçeği ve çakması — karşılayıcının hedeflerini daraltır, zayıf dönüşleri senin bitirişine çevirir.
takeawayTr: Serviste filede: topa dokunmasan bile her sayıda hareket et.

scenario: Returning in doubles against an active poacher at net. What's the discipline?
options: Crosscourt low over the middle, away from their reach — and lob early to back them off
Down their alley every time to punish
High floaters crosscourt
explanation: Low crosscourt is the percentage return; an EARLY lob (not a desperate one) plants doubt that freezes their poaching for the rest of the set.
takeaway: Beat poachers with low balls + one early lob message.
mistakeType: floating returns to an active net player
scenarioTr: Çiftlerde filede aktif poach yapan birine karşı karşılama yapıyorsun. Disiplin ne?
optionsTr: Ortadan alçak çapraz, uzanamayacağı yere — ve erkenden lob atıp geri it
explanationTr: Alçak çapraz yüzdeli karşılamadır; ERKEN atılan lob (çaresiz olan değil) akla şüphe eker ve set boyu poach'unu dondurur.
takeawayTr: Poach'çuyu alçak toplar + bir erken lob mesajıyla yen.

scenario: You want to poach more. What's the highest-percentage moment to go?
options: When your partner's serve jams the returner — body or strong T serve
Randomly, to stay unpredictable
Only when the returner looks tired
explanation: Poaching succeeds off predictable weak returns. A body/T serve compresses the returner, making the reply float toward the middle — your interception lane.
takeaway: Poach off the serve you KNOW creates a weak middle return.
mistakeType: random poaching without a serve plan
scenarioTr: Daha çok poach yapmak istiyorsun. En yüksek yüzdeli an hangisi?
optionsTr: Partnerinin servisi karşılayıcıyı sıkıştırdığında — gövde ya da sağlam T
explanationTr: Poach, tahmin edilebilir zayıf dönüşlerden beslenir. Gövde/T servisi karşılayıcıyı sıkıştırır; cevap ortaya süzülür — senin kesme koridorun.
takeawayTr: Zayıf orta dönüş yaratacağını BİLDİĞİN servisin üstüne poach yap.

scenario: Lob sails over your net-playing partner's head. Whose ball is it?
options: Call it, cross behind, partner switches sides
Your partner back-pedals for their own smash
Let it bounce, then take it from the baseline
explanation: The un-lobbed player has the shorter path and a forward view of the ball, so calling and crossing keeps the team facing the right way. Letting it bounce is playable, but it hands the net back and turns your team defensive for the rest of the point.
takeaway: Lob over your partner? Call it, cross, and switch as a unit.

scenario: Your team keeps losing from the one-up-one-back formation. What's the structural issue?
options: The huge diagonal gap between you — good teams attack the middle seam relentlessly
Not enough alley coverage
The net player stands too close
explanation: One-up-one-back concedes the middle diagonal. Winning doubles converges: both up when attacking (or both back defending) closes the seam.
takeaway: Doubles is won side-by-side, not corner-to-corner.
scenarioTr: Takımın biri-önde-biri-geride düzeninden sürekli kaybediyor. Yapısal sorun ne?
optionsTr: Aranızdaki dev diyagonal boşluk — iyi takımlar orta dikişe acımasızca saldırır
explanationTr: Biri-önde-biri-geride orta diyagonali hediye eder. Kazanan çiftler yakınsar: hücumda ikisi önde (savunmada ikisi geride) dikişi kapatır.
takeawayTr: Çiftler köşeden köşeye değil, yan yana kazanılır.

scenario: Serving and coming in, first volley in doubles with all four players active. Default target?
options: Low through the middle — between the opponents
Sharp angle to the alley
At the net player's body
explanation: The middle volley creates 'yours/mine' confusion, passes over the lowest net, and can't be angled away against you like an alley attempt.
takeaway: In doubles, the middle is a third opponent — recruit it.
scenarioTr: Servis atıp giriyorsun; dört oyuncu da aktifken çiftlerdeki ilk vole. Varsayılan hedef?
explanationTr: Orta vole 'senin mi benim mi' karmaşası yaratır, filenin en alçak yerinden geçer ve koridor denemesi gibi açıyla cezalandırılamaz.
takeawayTr: Çiftlerde orta üçüncü rakiptir — onu takımına al.

scenario: You're crouched on the centre line in I-formation at 30–40, and your partner will serve up the T. The returner has chipped every return crosscourt so far. When do you break?
options: Break as the serve lands
Break after the return is struck
Break as the toss goes up
explanation: Breaking as the serve lands puts you on the chip while the returner has already committed to their target. Moving on the toss is the classic error: the returner sees you go and simply redirects into the half you left.
takeaway: In the I, commit when the serve lands.
mistakeType: static formations against a grooved returner

scenario: 5–5 and you and your partner are both back. You've just clashed rackets on a ball down the middle for the second time this set, and neither of you said a word before the collision.
options: Call every ball early, before it lands
Call only the balls between you
Agree the forehand takes the middle
explanation: Calling every ball, even the obvious ones, builds the reflex that fires on the ambiguous one under pressure. Calling only the middle balls sounds efficient, but that call arrives after you have both already started moving.
takeaway: Call every ball, so the hard one gets called too.

scenario: The server rushes the net behind every serve. Your best repeated return?
options: Low at the incoming server's feet — make the first volley an upward defensive one
High and deep to the baseline
Hard at the net player
explanation: Their momentum forward makes ankle-height balls brutal: the first volley pops UP, and your partner at net feasts on it.
takeaway: Against rushing servers: return to shoelaces, partner cleans up.
scenarioTr: Servisçi her servisin arkasından fileye koşuyor. En iyi tekrarlanan karşılaman?
optionsTr: Gelen servisçinin ayak dibine alçak — ilk voleyi yukarı doğru savunmaya zorla
explanationTr: Öne momentumu, bilek hizası topları acımasız yapar: ilk vole YUKARI kalkar ve filedeki partnerin onunla ziyafet çeker.
takeawayTr: Koşan servisçiye: ayakkabı bağına dön, partner temizlesin.

scenario: 4–4, you're at the net and your partner is dragged wide off the ad corner chasing a lob. Both opponents are at the net waiting, and your partner can only float it back.
options: Cross to the open half and back up a step
Hold your side and stay tight to the net
Retreat to the baseline on your own side
explanation: Your partner will come back across behind you, so crossing covers the empty half and the extra step gives you room to answer the smash. Holding your side leaves half the court open and makes you the easiest target on it.
takeaway: When your partner is dragged off court, switch with them.
mistakeType: leaving a partner hanging at net

scenario: Deuce court at 30–30, partner at the net looking to poach. The returner runs around everything to hit forehands and has already burned your partner with two sharp crosscourt returns.
options: Serve T and let your partner poach
Serve wide and cover the crosscourt yourself
Serve into the body to jam the run-around
explanation: A T serve takes the crosscourt angle away and funnels the return through the middle, which is your net partner's kill zone. Serving wide opens the exact sharp angle that has already beaten your partner twice.
takeaway: Serve where your partner can poach, not where you must chase.
mistakeType: wide serves that expose the net partner

scenario: You return on the ad side at 30–40 (break point for your team). The alley is 'open'. What's the discipline?
options: Low crosscourt at the net player's feet
Drive it down the open alley
Lob over the net player's shoulder
explanation: An 'open' alley on break point is usually bait from a net player who intends to cover it, and a low crosscourt at their feet makes them play up from below the tape. The alley drive is the shot they are inviting.
takeaway: An open alley on a big point is an invitation — decline it.
mistakeType: taking the alley bait on big points

scenario: Your partner gets pulled wide to their forehand. What do YOU do at net?
options: Shift the same direction, covering the middle they just opened
Hold your position exactly
Drift to the opposite alley
explanation: Doubles pairs are roped together: when one slides wide, the middle opens unless the partner slides with them. The seam is always the first target.
takeaway: Move WITH your partner — the rope between you must never slack.
scenarioTr: Partnerin forehand tarafına, açığa çekildi. Sen filede ne yaparsın?
optionsTr: Aynı yöne kay, az önce açılan ortayı kapat
explanationTr: Çift oyuncuları birbirine iple bağlıdır: biri açığa kayınca partner birlikte kaymazsa orta açılır. Dikiş her zaman ilk hedeftir.
takeawayTr: Partnerinle BİRLİKTE kay — aranızdaki ip asla gevşemesin.

scenario: Your team hits a heavy approach and the opponents are scrambling deep. What's the winning team shape?
options: BOTH players close to the net — cut every angle, ready for the weak reply
One up, one back for lob insurance
Both retreat to mid-court
explanation: Against a scrambling defense, the reply is weak and floaty far more often than a perfect lob. Two players tight at net make the court disappear.
takeaway: When they scramble, you swarm — close together, finish together.
scenarioTr: Takımınız ağır bir yaklaşma vurdu, rakipler derinde debeleniyor. Kazanan takım şekli ne?
optionsTr: İKİ oyuncu da fileye — her açıyı kes, zayıf cevabı bekle
Lob sigortası için biri önde biri geride
explanationTr: Debelenen savunmanın cevabı, kusursuz lobdan çok daha sık zayıf ve süzülendir. Filede iki sıkı oyuncu kortu yok eder.
takeawayTr: Onlar debelenirken siz üşüşün — birlikte kapanın, birlikte bitirin.
